12.15.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: LTA 1954 — SECURITY OF TENURE: Business tenants with a tenancy under Part II of the Landlord and Tenant Act 1954 have the right to renew the tenancy at the end of the contractual term. The tenancy continues automatically at the end of the term (s.24 'holding over') unless either party serves notice.

GROUNDS OF OPPOSITION (s.30(1)): The landlord can oppose renewal on 7 grounds (a)-(g): (a)-(e) fault-based (disrepair, persistent rent arrears, substantial breaches, alternative accommodation offered, uneconomic sub-letting); (f) landlord intends to demolish/reconstruct; (g) landlord intends to occupy for own business/residence. Only grounds (f) and (g) require compensation if they succeed.

CONTRACTING OUT — EXCLUSION OF SECURITY OF TENURE: Since June 2004, the landlord must serve a notice warning the tenant of the consequences of contracting out. The tenant must make a statutory declaration (or sworn declaration) that they have received the notice and understand its effect. The lease then contains an agreement excluding the 1954 Act. The court order requirement was abolished.
RENEWAL RENT: The court sets the renewal rent on the basis of the market rent (assuming an open market letting) at the date of the renewal. Improvements carried out by the tenant are disregarded.

SECTION 25 NOTICE (LANDLORD) vs SECTION 26 REQUEST (TENANT): s.25: landlord serves notice to terminate the current tenancy (friendly if renewing offered; hostile if opposing). s.26: tenant serves request for new tenancy. BOTH must be for a date not less than 6 months and not more than 12 months from the notice/request date.

LANDLORD'S COMPENSATION: If the landlord successfully opposes renewal on grounds (f) or (g), the tenant is entitled to compensation. The amount depends on the rateable value and the time the tenant has been in occupation (1× or 2× rateable value depending on length of occupation).

12.14.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: FORM TR1: On assignment of existing registered lease, purchase deed = Form TR1 (transfer deed). NOT a new lease deed. Exception: unregistered lease <7 years may use a deed of assignment.

NOTICE OF ASSIGNMENT: After completion, tenant's solicitor MUST serve notice of assignment on landlord. Mandatory on assignment — does NOT apply to grant (landlord was party to grant). Also serve notice of charge (notice of mortgage) if buyer has a mortgage.
SDLT/LTT ON ASSIGNMENT: Payable on purchase price only. NO additional SDLT/LTT on rent (unlike grant of new lease where NPV of rent may generate additional liability).

LICENCE TO ASSIGN: Landlord's consent document. Required if lease contains alienation covenant. Landlord's legal fees = paid by outgoing tenant. Solicitor gives undertaking for costs — MUST have cleared funds before giving undertaking.
AGA ON ASSIGNMENT (new lease): Landlord may require outgoing T to enter AGA guaranteeing immediate assignee. Must be in lease. AGA expires when assignee further assigns.
DEED OF VARIATION: To change existing lease terms — requires landlord's agreement + deed of variation.
LICENCE TO UNDERLET: Landlord, tenant and subtenant ALL sign — creates privity of contract between all three. Subtenant registers underlease at HMLR if >7 years.
SERVICE CHARGE/RENT APPORTIONMENTS: Apportioned at completion. Check ground rent + service charge receipts from seller.

12.13.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: TERMS FIXED AT EXCHANGE: Once a contract/agreement for lease with a draft lease attached has been EXCHANGED, the terms CANNOT be changed. Amendment requires landlord's agreement + deed of variation.

ENGROSSMENT — TWO PARTS: Original (signed by LANDLORD) + counterpart (signed by TENANT + guarantor if any). At completion, parties SWAP — tenant holds original; landlord holds counterpart. Both end up with identical copy signed by the other.

SDLT/LTT ON GRANT: Payable on the PREMIUM (purchase price) in usual way PLUS if NPV of total rent over lease term exceeds the threshold: ADDITIONAL SDLT/LTT payable on rent element. This differs from an ASSIGNMENT where SDLT/LTT is on purchase price only.

AGREEMENT FOR LEASE: Binding contract to grant a lease at a future date. If specific performance possible = equitable leasehold interest. Register as notice (registered) or Class C(iv) land charge (unregistered) to protect against third parties.
LANDLORD'S MORTGAGE: If landlord's title is mortgaged, must obtain lender's consent to grant of lease.
UNDERLEASE MUST BE SHORTER: Underlease must be shorter in duration than residue of head lease.
UNDERTAKING FOR COSTS: Solicitor must have CLEARED FUNDS from client before giving undertaking to pay landlord's legal fees for any licence/consent.

12.12.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: OLD vs NEW LEASE: Date of LEASE GRANT (not date of assignment) determines which rules apply. Old = granted before 1 January 1996. New = granted on or after 1 January 1996.
OLD LEASE LIABILITY: Original T remains liable for ENTIRE term — even after multiple assignments. L can pursue T1 for T4's rent even if T1 assigned in 1992.
NEW LEASE — AUTOMATIC RELEASE: T automatically released on assignment. But assignor remains liable for breaches occurring WHILE they were the tenant.

AGA: Commercial leases — landlord may require outgoing T to enter AGA. Must be provided for in the lease. Guarantees IMMEDIATE assignee's performance ONLY — expires when that assignee further assigns.
AGA VOID IF: Attempts to impose greater liability on outgoing T than contained in the lease itself.
NO AUTOMATIC LANDLORD RELEASE: Landlord is NOT automatically released from covenants under LTCA 1995.
s.146 NOTICE: Required before forfeiture for any non-rent covenant breach — must specify breach, require remedy (if capable), require compensation.
CRAR: Commercial Rent Arrears Recovery — available in COMMERCIAL leases ONLY. NOT available if any part of the property is let as a dwelling.

WAIVER OF THE RIGHT TO FORFEIT: waiver occurs where the landlord (1) KNOWS of the tenant’s breach, (2) does something or takes steps recognising that the LEASE CONTINUES, and (3) COMMUNICATES that act to the tenant. Demanding or accepting rent after becoming aware of the breach can amount to waiver.

SUING A FORMER TENANT — 6 MONTHS: on a debt action the landlord can recover only 6 YEARS’ arrears (Limitation Act 1980 s 19); and to sue a FORMER tenant the landlord must serve notice within 6 MONTHS of the breach occurring.

RELIEF FROM FORFEITURE: for non-payment of rent, paying all arrears and the landlord’s costs usually lets the tenant keep the lease. For other breaches the tenant may apply for relief under LPA 1925 s 146(2) at any time before the landlord re-enters — but NOT unless the breach has been remedied. Under s 146(4) a SUBTENANT may apply for relief if the head lease is forfeited, and if successful becomes the immediate tenant of the head landlord for the residue of the sublease term.

12.11.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: REGISTRATION: Lease >7 years = compulsorily registrable at HMLR — new leasehold title + title number created. Short particulars on Property Register (date, term, rent, parties) NEVER CHANGE even after assignment.

GROUND RENT CAP: LRGRA 2022 in force 22 June 2022 — residential leases >21 years: rent limited to peppercorn (effectively nil). NOT retrospective (leases before 22 June 2022 unaffected UNLESS varied or extended after).

ALIENATION COVENANTS: Absolute (no assignment) — LTA 1927 s.19(1)(a) has NO effect. Qualified (consent required) — s.19(1)(a) converts to FULLY QUALIFIED (consent not unreasonably withheld). s.19(1A) [commercial only]: landlord may specify conditions for consent to assign in advance.
FORFEITURE — NOT AUTOMATIC: Landlord can only forfeit if: (1) express right of re-entry in lease, OR (2) tenant's obligation is a condition. Must be exercised — NOT automatic.
WAIVER: Landlord waives forfeiture if they KNOW of breach AND demand/accept rent (or take other act recognising lease continues) AND communicate this to tenant.
EFFLUXION OF TIME: Fixed-term lease expires automatically — no notice needed (unless LTA 1954 protects business tenant).
SURRENDER: Written agreement enforceable in equity OR estoppel (landlord accepts possession at tenant's request).
MERGER: Tenant acquires reversion → leasehold interest merges with freehold. Tenant cannot be own landlord.

12.10.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: COMPLETION TIME: Standard Conditions and SCPC require completion by 2PM on completion date. Completion after 2pm = deemed to be next working day.
NO COMPLETION DATE IN CONTRACT: Standard Conditions and SCPC provide default = 20 WORKING DAYS from exchange of contracts.
DELAYED COMPLETION ≠ RIGHT TO RESCIND: Time is NOT of the essence under Standard Conditions/SCPC. Delay alone does not entitle innocent party to refuse to complete.

NOTICE TO COMPLETE: Innocent party must be READY, ABLE AND WILLING to complete before serving notice. If buyer defaults after notice: seller keeps DEPOSIT, resells, claims damages. If seller defaults: buyer gets deposit back WITH INTEREST + damages.
NOTICE PERIOD: 10 working days (excluding day of service). During notice period, time is of the essence.
REDUCED DEPOSIT: If buyer paid a reduced deposit on exchange, serving a notice to complete requires the buyer to immediately TOP UP to 10%.

MISREPRESENTATION: False statement of fact by one party or their agent that induces the other to enter the contract. Fraudulent = damages + rescission. Negligent = damages OR rescission. Innocent = rescission only (damages at court's discretion under MA 1967 s.2(2)).
POST-COMPLETION REMEDIES LIMITED: Most contract terms merge with the purchase deed on completion. Only breach of title guarantee covenants and misrepresentation survive.

12.9.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: SDLT / LTT — FILING DEADLINES: SDLT must be paid to HMRC within 14 days of completion (England). LTT must be paid to WRA within 30 days of completion (Wales). The SDLT5 certificate (or LTT receipt) must be lodged with HMLR to register the title.

REGISTRATION — POST-COMPLETION: The buyer's solicitor must apply to HMLR within the OS1 priority period. Failure to register = the legal title does not pass. Late registration = the priority period is lost; a new entry may have been made in the interim.

COMPLETION — LAW SOCIETY CODE FOR COMPLETION BY POST: Completion occurs when the seller's solicitor's bank account is credited with the balance of the purchase price. The seller's solicitor must IMMEDIATELY release keys/title documents on receiving confirmation of receipt. Acting as agent for the buyer.

UNDERTAKINGS: A solicitor's undertaking is a personal, professional obligation. If the solicitor gives an undertaking (e.g., to discharge a mortgage on completion), they are personally liable if they do not comply, regardless of whether the client provides funds. Undertakings should only be given if the solicitor can ensure compliance.

TRANSFER DEED: In registered land, a TR1 (or TR2 for part of land) is the transfer document. It must be executed as a deed (signed, witnessed, delivered). The transfer vests the legal estate in the buyer only on registration at HMLR.

REQUISITIONS ON TITLE: Before completion, the buyer's solicitor raises formal enquiries (requisitions) on the title (Form TA13) and requires undertakings regarding discharge of mortgages and other incumbrances.

12.8.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: EXCHANGE, NOT COMPLETION, is the point at which the matter becomes LEGALLY BINDING. Work out where in the transaction the scenario sits - everything in the report to the buyer is PRE-exchange.
BEFORE EXCHANGE either party can withdraw with NO legal consequence or penalty to the other - they may owe their OWN solicitor's fees per the client care letter.
DEPOSIT: typically 10% of the PURCHASE PRICE and paid on EXCHANGE, not completion. It must be CLEARED funds in client account - relying on uncleared funds breaches the SRA Accounts Rules.
POSTAL EXCHANGE: the transaction becomes binding when the SELLER'S part of the contract is POSTED to the buyer's solicitor - not on receipt, and not when the buyer's part is posted.
THREE Ps (methods: phone, post, person) are NOT the three FORMULAE (A, B, C). The formulae apply only to exchange BY PHONE. Do not confuse them.
FORMULA C IS MANDATORY IN A CHAIN. Formula A is the answer where one solicitor holds both parts and the deposit, e.g. because a solicitor will not be in the office on the day.
FORM A RESTRICTION = TENANTS IN COMMON. No Form A = JOINT TENANTS. Unregistered title: read the conveyance.
SURVIVORSHIP beats the will. On a joint tenant's death the interest passes to the survivors with NO formality other than producing the DEATH CERTIFICATE - no grant needed for that interest.
TENANT IN COMMON DIES: check there are still TWO TRUSTEES of the legal estate to give a valid receipt so that beneficial interests OVERREACH. Only one survivor → APPOINT A SECOND TRUSTEE.
MAXIMUM FOUR legal owners, of full age and capacity, and the LEGAL estate can ONLY be held as JOINT TENANTS. Only the BENEFICIAL interest can be a tenancy in common.

RISK PASSES TO THE BUYER ON EXCHANGE under both the Standard Conditions and the SCPC - the buyer must complete even if the property is damaged or destroyed. Hence insurance on risk at exchange. The seller still owes a CONTINUING DUTY to keep the property in the same state as at exchange.
IRREVOCABLE AUTHORITY is needed from EVERY seller client and EVERY buyer client. Exchanging without it = negligence claim.

ESTATE CONTRACT: consider registering if MORE THAN 2-3 WEEKS between exchange and completion (classically a new build bought from a builder). Registered title → NOTICE on the seller's CHARGES register. Unregistered → C(iv) LAND CHARGE against the seller's FULL NAME. Remove it on completion.

SIMULTANEOUS EXCHANGE AND COMPLETION: there is NO period of binding contract beforehand, so EITHER PARTY CAN WITHDRAW WITHOUT PENALTY even on the chosen completion date. That is the drawback, not an advantage.

BUYER IN OCCUPATION BEFORE COMPLETION: the Standard Conditions let the buyer occupy as a LICENSEE. The SCPC contain NO such provision - in a commercial transaction a SPECIAL CONDITION must be negotiated before exchange.

12.7.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: BUYER CANNOT RELY ON THE MORTGAGE VALUATION REPORT: the valuation is carried out for the LENDER (to confirm the property is adequate security) even though the buyer pays for it. Classic trap: a structural defect (e.g. a large crack) appears after completion, the buyer commissioned no survey of their own and tries to rely on the valuation report — they cannot. Advise buyers to obtain their own survey (see 12.5).

GENERIC ADVICE ONLY (FSMA 2000): the solicitor may explain the terms and type of mortgage product but must NOT recommend a particular product or lender or comment on its suitability. If the client asks whether a product suits them, the solicitor must decline and refer them to an independent, suitably qualified mortgage adviser.

GIFTED DEPOSIT: where a third party (often a relative) contributes to the price, the buyer's solicitor must run the SAME source-of-funds and source-of-wealth checks on the donor, and the gift MUST be declared to the lender. The donor may acquire a beneficial interest, so the lender will usually require the donor (and any non-owning occupier) to sign a consent form agreeing to postpone their interest / vacate on repossession.

BUYER + LENDER — USUALLY NO CONFLICT: in most residential transactions the same solicitor acts for both, and there is no conflict because both want a good and marketable title. BUT if the buyer-borrower tells the solicitor not to disclose an adverse matter to the lender, a conflict arises — the solicitor must decline to act for the lender and return the mortgage instructions/offer.

COMPANY CHARGE — 21 DAYS: if the buyer is a limited company, the mortgage must ALSO be registered at Companies House within 21 days of completion. The deadline is strict — miss it and a court order is needed; the solicitor will be negligent. Look for the buyer described as 'Ltd' / 'Limited' / 'a company'.

CERTIFICATE OF TITLE: a standard-form document with two functions — (1) it requests drawdown of the mortgage advance and (2) it confirms to the lender that the title is good and marketable. The lender is entitled to rely on it.
MINIMUM LEASE TERM: lenders commonly require a minimum unexpired residential lease term (increasingly 85 years). A short residue can make the property unacceptable security.

REGISTER THE CHARGE / PRIORITY IN THE LENDER'S NAME: for registered land the pre-completion OS1 (or OS2) priority search must be in the LENDER's name and registration completed within the 30-working-day priority period; for unregistered land, first registration (which includes the charge) must be lodged within 2 months of completion.

12.6.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: WHAT IS DEVELOPMENT: Development requires planning permission. 'Development' means: (a) carrying out of building, engineering, mining or other operations; AND/OR (b) making of a material change in the use of any buildings or other land. Neither requires permission: maintenance/improvement works not materially affecting the external appearance; uses within the same use class.

PERMITTED DEVELOPMENT: Certain types of development are automatically permitted under the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) Order 2015 without the need for a planning application (e.g., small domestic extensions, minor works). Permitted development rights can be removed by conditions or Article 4 Directions.

ENFORCEMENT — TIME LIMITS: If development is carried out without permission, the local authority can serve an enforcement notice. Manual periods (same in England AND Wales): 4 years from the breach for building/operational works OR a change of use to a single dwelling house; 10 years for ALL other breaches (any other change of use; breach of a planning condition). If a breach has been deliberately concealed, there is NO time limit. After the limit expires the development becomes immune from planning enforcement.

BUILDING REGULATIONS — SEPARATE FROM PLANNING: Building regulations are separate from planning and cover health/safety of construction. Almost all building work needs building regulations consent EVEN IF it does not need planning permission (e.g., windows, electrical work, boilers). ⚠ Enforcement: from 1 Oct 2023 a LOCAL AUTHORITY has 10 years from completion to enforce — BUT that 10-year limit does NOT apply to the Building Safety Regulator (a 'building control authority'), which has NO time limit. Criminal prosecution: no time limit. Injunction: available at any time where there is a threat to public health.

LISTED BUILDINGS AND CONSERVATION AREAS: Unauthorized works to a listed building (alteration or demolition affecting character) = criminal offence. Works in a conservation area also require consent. Solicitors must check listings and check for any enforcement history.

12.5.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: LOCAL SEARCH SCOPE — ONLY THE ADDRESS SEARCHED AGAINST: the results give NO information about adjoining land. This is the important limitation of the search. A question about the neighbour's land requires a separate search of that address.

THE LOCAL SEARCH FALLS INTO TWO PARTS: and it is the LOCAL AUTHORITY that provides the information — roads maintenance, planning and building regulations, tree preservation orders, conservation area status.

DRAINAGE SEARCH IS OF THE UTILITY COMPANY: it reveals connection to the PUBLIC water supply and the PUBLIC FOUL drainage system. If the property is not connected, enquire as to the alternative — e.g. a private drainage system.
ENVIRONMENTAL SEARCH IS A DESKTOP SEARCH: contaminated land, flooding and soil type. It is not a physical inspection.

PHYSICAL INSPECTION IS DONE IN EVERY CASE: it is listed as one of the searches for every purchase — looking for third-party rights, occupiers and rights of way. CAVEAT EMPTOR is why the buyer must inspect and survey.
ONLY THE LENDER CAN RELY ON THE MORTGAGE VALUATION REPORT: even though the BUYER pays for it. The buyer can rely on the homebuyers' report and the full structural survey.

COAL MINING, CANAL/RIVER, CHANCEL, COMMONS ARE LOCATION-DRIVEN: read the facts for the trigger. Commons registration is one of the local authority OPTIONAL enquiries — optional enquiries are answered only if the applicant asks for them.

UNREGISTERED TITLE = SIM PLUS THE K15 LAND CHARGES OFFICIAL SEARCH: the index map search reveals whether all or part is already registered at HMLR or subject to a CAUTION AGAINST FIRST REGISTRATION. The K15 goes against the FULL NAMES of all estate owners since the ROOT OF TITLE, for the full years of their ownership.

K15 v K16: K15 is the LAND CHARGES OFFICIAL search against estate owners of an UNREGISTERED title, for their periods of ownership IN THE RELEVANT COUNTY. K16 is the BANKRUPTCY OFFICIAL search, for the LENDER against the BUYER'S name, repeated pre-completion (12.9).

WRONG SPELLING, WRONG PERIOD OR WRONG COUNTY DEFEATS THE SEARCH: the K15 goes against the correct spelling of the names, for the correct periods of ownership, IN THE RELEVANT COUNTY. Look for this in the facts.

DO NOT CONFUSE PRE-CONTRACT WITH PRE-COMPLETION SEARCHES: pre-contract searches are done BEFORE EXCHANGE; pre-completion searches (and their priority periods) are done between exchange and completion — see 12.9.
NO EXCHANGE UNTIL ENQUIRIES ARE SATISFIED: the buyer's solicitor cannot review the file and prepare for exchange until SATISFACTORY replies to ALL enquiries have been received.

'NOT SO FAR AS THE SELLER IS AWARE' IS UNWISE: it can be read as the seller confirming it has done its own due diligence with nothing to disclose. Qualify it with 'but the seller has not carried out any investigation in this respect'. Incorrect replies that INDUCE the buyer to proceed can found a MISREPRESENTATION claim.

TA6 v CPSE: the CPSE is the COMMERCIAL equivalent of the Property Information Form and is more comprehensive. The process of investigating title and raising enquiries is otherwise the SAME for a commercial transaction.
DS1 v DS3: DS1 releases the WHOLE of the land in a title from a mortgage; DS3 is the receipt releasing the PART being sold. Do not confuse them.
TR1 v TP1: TR1 transfers the whole; TP1 transfers part and carries the rights granted, the rights reserved for the retained land, and any covenants imposed on the buyer.
PLAN COLOURS: land SOLD is edged RED; land the seller keeps (the 'retained land') is edged BLUE. The plan must be HMLR-compliant, have a NORTH POINT and be to a recognised scale.
LENDER'S CONSENT ON A SALE OF PART: if the seller's title is in mortgage the lender must consent, because the part sold has to be released from the mortgage on completion.

NEW BUILD — SECTION 38 v SECTION 104: the agreement to build to a good and workmanlike standard is a SECTION 38 AGREEMENT for the ROADS and a SECTION 104 AGREEMENT for the WATER AND SEWER PIPES, each backed by a BOND. The LOCAL search reveals the road agreement and bond; the DRAINAGE search reveals the drainage agreement and bond.

NEW BUILD DEPOSIT IS OFTEN HELD AS AGENT, NOT STAKEHOLDER: stakeholder means the seller's solicitor holds it for both parties pending completion; agent means it can be paid straight to the seller. On a new build the seller usually insists on agent — so the buyer needs DEPOSIT PROTECTION in the warranty.
NEW BUILD WARRANTY RUNS FOR 10 YEARS: it covers STRUCTURAL DEFECTS and is in addition to the buildings insurance the buyer puts on risk at exchange. NHBC is the most common provider.

12.4.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: CLASSES OF REGISTERED TITLE: Absolute title (most common): HMLR guarantees the title. Good leasehold: HMLR does not guarantee the superior title (because it has not seen it). Qualified: registered subject to a particular defect. Possessory: based on adverse possession — the State guarantees only that no one has better title as of the date of registration.

REGISTERED vs UNREGISTERED TITLE: In unregistered land, title is proven by deduction through an abstract of title/epitome of title going back at least 15 years. All transactions with unregistered land trigger compulsory first registration. Searches of the Land Charges Register (not Land Registry) are needed for unregistered land.

items: Property Register: description and appurtenant rights
Proprietorship Register: class of title, name of owner, restrictions
Charges Register: incumbrances (mortgages, restrictions, covenants). Overriding interests do not appear on the register but bind the buyer without notice
body.head: THE THREE REGISTERS AT HMLR

body: OVERRIDING INTERESTS: Bind a buyer even though not entered on the register. Key examples: legal leases of 7 years or less; interests of persons in actual occupation (Schedule 3, para.2 LRA 2002 — buyer must make reasonable inquiries); legal easements and profits.

OFFICIAL COPIES vs OFFICE COPIES: Official copies of the register (downloaded from HMLR) are used for investigating title. They do not give the buyer a priority period — an OS1 or OS2 search is needed for that.

FIRST REGISTRATION: Application must be made within 2 months of the trigger event (sale, first legal mortgage, gift, court order, etc.). If not made in time, the legal title reverts to the transferor who then holds it on trust for the transferee.

12.3.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: DEPOSIT IS HELD AS STAKEHOLDER, NOT AGENT. The seller's solicitor holds it in the firm's client account on behalf of BOTH parties pending completion, and pays it to the seller ON COMPLETION. Holding as AGENT - which lets the seller have it immediately after exchange - is the EXCEPTION, typically pushed by a DEVELOPER selling a new build, and the buyer's solicitor should resist it. [CORRECTED: this section previously stated the opposite.]

FULL TITLE GUARANTEE IS THE DEFAULT under BOTH the Standard Conditions and the SCPC. If the seller is not an owner-occupier, their solicitor MUST amend the front page. Fail to amend and the seller is assumed to give a FULL guarantee. Personal representative → LIMITED. Mortgagee in possession → NONE.

PATENT v LATENT: patent defects (apparent on inspection, e.g. a visible right of way) need NOT be disclosed - caveat emptor. LATENT defects (e.g. a restrictive covenant) MUST be disclosed in the contract. Do not reverse these.
THE CONTRACTUAL DUTY OF DISCLOSURE IS NARROW. The seller's real exposure is MISREPRESENTATION via the TA6 and replies to pre-contract enquiries - not the contract.

CHATTELS OVERVALUATION IS FRAUD. SDLT / LTT is payable only on the consideration for the LAND, so the fittings and contents sum is shown separately - but it must be the TRUE MARKET VALUE. Inflating it and correspondingly reducing the price is FRAUD on HMRC or the Welsh Revenue Authority, and the SOLICITORS COULD BE COMPLICIT. Watch for a scenario paying over market value for fittings.

RISK IS NOT AN OBLIGATION TO INSURE. Risk passes to the buyer on EXCHANGE, so the buyer must complete even if the building is damaged or destroyed - but the Standard Conditions do NOT require the buyer to insure. A prudent buyer insures as a precaution.
ANYTHING AGREED BETWEEN THE PARTIES MUST GO IN AS A SPECIAL CONDITION or it is NOT binding - down to the washing machine.

A REDUCED DEPOSIT IS THE SELLER'S RISK: on the buyer's default the seller is entitled to the FULL 10%, but if the buyer cannot fund the shortfall the seller will struggle to recover it. Explain this to the seller.

CONTRACT RATE is a PENALTY rate of interest for LATE COMPLETION, inserted by the seller's solicitor by reference to their own bank. The BUYER'S solicitor should amend anything more than 4% or 5% above base rate as too punitive.

VAT IS A COMMERCIAL ISSUE ONLY. Commercial building sold WITHIN 3 YEARS of construction = standard rated. Older property = the seller has the OPTION TO TAX, which hurts a buyer who is not VAT registered and cannot recover it. If the contract says the price is "INCLUSIVE OF VAT", the seller CANNOT add VAT later.

CONDITIONAL CONTRACT = CONDITION PRECEDENT: there is NO binding contract until the condition is satisfied, so the buyer can walk away without penalty. Rarely used residentially and NEVER where either party has a related transaction.
SURVIVING TENANT IN COMMON CANNOT SELL ALONE. A second trustee must be appointed IN THE TRANSFER to overreach. A surviving beneficial JOINT tenant CAN sell alone - just send the death certificate.
MORTGAGEE IN POSSESSION: the buyer must check the power of sale EXISTS AND HAS ARISEN and see the COURT ORDER FOR POSSESSION.

REDEMPTION SHORTFALL COMES OUT OF THE FIRM'S OWN MONEY. If the seller's solicitor gives the undertaking to redeem but lacks the funds on completion, they are in BREACH and the buyer's solicitor can require the firm to make up the shortfall itself. Manual example: sale £150,000, mortgage £170,000 - a £20,000 shortfall, before legal and estate agent's fees.

12.2.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: SDLT vs LTT — WHICH APPLIES: SDLT (paid to HMRC) applies to properties in ENGLAND. LTT (paid to WRA) applies to properties in WALES. The test is the location of the property — not the nationality of the buyer or the location of the solicitors. Scotland has its own LBTT; Northern Ireland uses SDLT.

NOTIFICATION THRESHOLD vs PAYMENT THRESHOLD: A buyer must NOTIFY HMRC/WRA of any transaction with consideration of £40,000 or more — even if NO tax is due. Payment of SDLT only arises where the price exceeds £125,000 (residential England) or £225,000 (residential Wales). A buyer of a £80,000 house in England must file an SDLT1 but pays £0 SDLT.

COMMERCIAL vs RESIDENTIAL RATES: Different rate bands apply depending on whether the property is residential or non-residential (commercial/mixed-use). Mixed-use property (any commercial element) and purchases of 6 or more residential properties in a single transaction are treated as NON-RESIDENTIAL for SDLT/LTT purposes — commercial rates apply.

HRAD SURCHARGE: The +5% Higher Rates for Additional Dwellings (SDLT) applies to any individual purchasing an additional residential property who will own more than one after completion. Companies buying ANY residential property pay HRAD even if it is their first. Exception: if the buyer is replacing their main residence and the previous one sold within 36 months.

FILING DEADLINES — DO NOT CONFUSE: SDLT: 14 days from completion to submit SDLT1 and pay. LTT: 30 DAYS from completion to submit LTT return and pay. The SDLT5 certificate (England) and LTT receipt (Wales) are required by HMLR before the title can be registered.

CGT ON PROPERTY DISPOSALS: UK residents pay CGT on gains from UK property at 18% (basic rate) or 24% (higher rate) for residential property. Non-UK residents pay CGT on ALL UK property gains. 60-day reporting and payment rule: CGT on UK residential property (both residents and non-residents) must be reported and paid within 60 days of completion.

12.1.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors

items: there is a specific enquiry,
a trap is deliberately concealed, or
there is misrepresentation. Non-disclosure of a defect the seller knows about (but did not create) does not itself give rise to liability
body.head: CAVEAT EMPTOR: The buyer is responsible for investigating the physical condition and legal status of the property. The seller has no general duty to disclose defects UNLESS

body: PROTOCOL FORMS: For residential transactions, the National Conveyancing Protocol requires the seller's solicitor to provide TA6 (Property Information Form), TA10 (Fittings and Contents Form), and (for leasehold) TA7. These are the seller's duty of disclosure forms.

EXCHANGE vs COMPLETION: Exchange of contracts creates a binding contract — neither party can withdraw without penalty. Completion is when title passes and the money is paid. There is usually a gap between exchange and completion (typically 1-4 weeks for residential). The risk in the property passes to the buyer on exchange (unless the Standard Conditions provide otherwise).

SOLICITOR'S OBLIGATIONS ON EXCHANGE: The solicitor must ensure their client understands the consequences of exchange. Once exchange has occurred, neither party can pull out without being in breach. A solicitor who exchanges without authority is in breach of duty.

THE CHAIN: In a chain of transactions, all exchanges must occur simultaneously or the chain collapses. Law Society Formulae (A, B, C) provide mechanisms for simultaneous exchange. Formula B is most common in residential chains.

JOINT OWNERSHIP — FORMS: Co-owners hold the legal title as joint tenants (Law of Property Act 1925 imposes a trust of land). Beneficial ownership can be as joint tenants or tenants in common. Solicitors must advise on the difference and take client instructions — particularly important to advise on when one party contributes more than 50%.

CPSE vs PROPERTY INFORMATION FORM — COMMERCIAL vs RESIDENTIAL: In a COMMERCIAL transaction, pre-contract enquiries are answered using the COMMERCIAL PROPERTY STANDARD ENQUIRIES (CPSE). The Property Information Form (TA6) and Leasehold Information Form are RESIDENTIAL forms only. Never use residential forms for commercial property questions. See 12.1.6.

SYNCHRONIZED COMPLETION — EXACT TERM: When a buyer is also selling their existing home and wants both transactions to complete on the SAME DAY, this is called 'SYNCHRONIZED' completion. Not 'simultaneous', not 'concurrent', not 'contemporaneous'. This is a frequently tested vocabulary trap. See 12.1.3.1.

4.6.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: OLD v NEW LEASE — TENANT: dated BEFORE 1 January 1996, the original tenant remains liable for the tenant covenants for the ENTIRE term even after assignment. Dated ON OR AFTER 1 January 1996, the original tenant is RELEASED on assignment — unless the lease requires an authorised guarantee agreement.
AGA IS LIMITED TO THE IMMEDIATE ASSIGNEE: the outgoing tenant guarantees the incoming tenant only for the period THAT assignee holds the lease.

OLD v NEW LEASE — LANDLORD: on a sale of the freehold reversion under a NEW lease the landlord is NOT automatically released. It must take an INDEMNITY from the buyer, an EXPRESS RELEASE from the tenant, or use the LTCA STATUTORY RELEASE procedure.
RENT IS NO LONGER A REQUIREMENT OF A LEASE: [Street v Mountford] lists exclusive legal possession of defined premises, for a term certain, at a rent — but technically rent is no longer required.

TERM CERTAIN — 'FOR THE DURATION OF THE WAR' IS NOT: it must be possible at CREATION to identify when the lease will end [Lace v Chantler]. 'Whilst King Charles III is on the throne' fails for the same reason.
THE LABEL DOES NOT DECIDE IT: an arrangement called a 'lease' that lacks the elements is only a LICENCE — a personal right that does not bind third parties.

SHORT LEASE — FOUR CONDITIONS AND THE ASSIGNMENT TRAP: 3 YEARS OR LESS may be created in writing or ORALLY only if the tenant TAKES POSSESSION, at the BEST RENT reasonably obtainable, with NO premium or fine, and (being under 7 years) it is an OVERRIDING INTEREST binding the legal owner and any buyer. Even so it can be ASSIGNED ONLY BY DEED.

LEASES OF 7 YEARS OR LESS ARE OVERRIDING INTERESTS: a 3–7 year legal lease MAY be noted on the charges register, but it binds the buyer WHETHER NOTED OR NOT. Being under 7 years is also the FOURTH condition for a short lease created without a deed.

DAMAGES FOR DISREPAIR ARE CAPPED AT THE DIMINUTION IN THE REVERSION: LTA 1927 s 18 — which is why the landlord prefers the 'Jervis v Harris' self-help route, recovering the cost as a DEBT and avoiding the cap.
s 146 COUNTER-NOTICE — 3 OR MORE YEARS UNEXPIRED: the tenant may serve a counter-notice, and if it does the landlord cannot take any further action WITHOUT THE LEAVE OF THE COURT.
UNREGISTERED LAND, LEASE OVER 7 YEARS: apply for substantive registration WITHIN 2 MONTHS of completion — even though the freehold title itself is unregistered.
EQUITABLE LEASE OUT OF AN UNREGISTERED TITLE: register against the NAME of the unregistered freeholder as a C(iv) land charge (estate contract). Registration constitutes notice.

FORFEITURE CLAUSE IS NEVER IMPLIED: it must be EXPRESSLY included. Peaceable re-entry also needs express provision and is NOT permitted for residential premises, which require a court order: Protection from Eviction Act 1977 s 1.
s 146 NOTICE — EVERY BREACH EXCEPT RENT ARREARS: it warns the tenant and allows a reasonable time to rectify IF the breach is capable of remedy; forfeiture may be commenced on expiry.

CRAR APPLIES WITHOUT BEING IN THE LEASE: all new AND existing COMMERCIAL leases from 6 April 2014, whether or not the lease refers to it. It replaced distress — but the tenant must be given NOTICE first.
SELF-HELP RECOVERS A DEBT, NOT DAMAGES: under a 'Jervis v Harris' clause the landlord enters, carries out the repairs and recovers the cost from the tenant AS A DEBT.

s 19(3) LTA 1927 DOES NOT HELP THE TENANT ON CHANGE OF USE: it imposes NO duty on the landlord not to withhold consent unreasonably to a change of use of business premises — it merely limits the terms on which consent may be granted. Contrast s 19, which DOES prevent unreasonable withholding of consent to ASSIGNMENT under a qualified covenant.
s 19(1A) IS COMMERCIAL AND POST-1995 ONLY: pre-agreed conditions for consent to assignment apply to commercial leases granted on or after 1 January 1996.

LTA 1954 — WHICH GROUNDS ARE MANDATORY: (a), (b), (c) and (e) are DISCRETIONARY (the court may order a new tenancy anyway); (d), (f) and (g) are MANDATORY (the court MUST refuse). Do not assume fault grounds are the mandatory ones.

LTA 1954 — COMPENSATION FOLLOWS (e), (f) AND (g) ONLY: the no-fault grounds. Nothing on (a), (b), (c) (fault) or (d) (no loss). Statutory formula; may be excluded by agreement, typically in the lease.
OPPOSED s 25 NOTICE = 6 TO 12 MONTHS: and it must specify the s 30 ground(s). On a tenant's s 26 request the LANDLORD has 2 MONTHS to say whether it opposes.
LTA 1954 DOES NOT APPLY TO FIXED TERMS OF 6 MONTHS OR LESS: nor to agricultural tenancies or contracted-out tenancies.

CONTRACTING OUT — SIMPLE OR STATUTORY DECLARATION: health warning MORE than 14 days before the tenant commits = SIMPLE declaration; LESS than 14 days = STATUTORY declaration before an INDEPENDENT SOLICITOR. The lease must refer to all three elements. Failure = contracting out VOID.
COURT-ORDERED NEW LEASE: maximum fixed term the court can order is 15 YEARS, and the new lease does not commence until 3 MONTHS after the proceedings are finally disposed of.

body: ETRIDGE EXTENDED TO HYBRID TRANSACTIONS: the Etridge principles now also apply where only PART of the loan is for the sole benefit of one of the parties — a HYBRID transaction (One Savings Bank Plc v Waller-Edwards). The lender is therefore put on inquiry in that case too, and must take the Etridge steps.

4.5.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: POSITIVE COVENANT BURDEN DOES NOT RUN — at law OR in equity (Rhone v Stephens). Only the RESTRICTIVE (negative) burden runs, and only in EQUITY (Tulk v Moxhay). Test the SUBSTANCE, not the wording: 'not to let the fence fall into disrepair' is POSITIVE (costs money to comply) despite starting 'not to'.

EASEMENT vs LICENCE: an easement is proprietary and binds successors; a licence is personal. Apply the Re Ellenborough Park criteria — a right that doesn't accommodate the land (e.g. Hill v Tupper, sole right to put boats on a canal for business) is a mere licence.

WHEELDON v BURROWS vs s.62: Wheeldon operates on a GRANT only (not reservation) and needs the quasi-easement to be continuous & apparent, necessary for reasonable enjoyment, and in use at transfer. s.62 (LPA 1925) upgrades a privilege/informal right into a full easement on a CONVEYANCE — and can be expressly excluded.

POWER OF SALE — TWO SEPARATE STAGES. (1) It ARISES (s.101) once the mortgage is by deed AND the money is 'due' — the deed fixes a legal redemption date, conventionally ~6 months after creation; once that date passes the money is 'due' (a technical trigger, NOT actual default). (2) It becomes EXERCISABLE (s.103) only once ONE trigger is met: notice to repay served and unmet after 3 months; OR interest is 2 months or more in arrears; OR breach of another mortgage term. So the ~6-month redemption date makes it ARISE; the 2 months' arrears is a s.103 EXERCISABLE trigger — different stages. Selling after it has arisen but before any s.103 trigger STILL passes good title to a bona fide buyer (s.104) — the mortgagor's only remedy is damages. A buyer checks it AROSE (s.101), not that s.103 was satisfied.

FORECLOSURE vs POWER OF SALE — SURPLUS: on a POWER OF SALE any surplus is held ON TRUST for later mortgagees then the borrower. On FORECLOSURE (rare, court order) the lender KEEPS the property/surplus. Don't mix them up.

PUISNE MORTGAGE: a LEGAL mortgage of UNREGISTERED land not protected by deposit of title deeds (i.e. a second/later mortgage) must be registered as a C(i) LAND CHARGE to bind. An equitable mortgage of unregistered land = C(iii) land charge.

NON-OWNING OCCUPIER: a spouse who contributed to the purchase price AND is in occupation can have an OVERRIDING INTEREST binding the lender (Williams & Glyn's Bank v Boland) — hence lenders require occupiers to sign a consent/waiver. Consent procured by undue influence can be set aside (O'Brien; Etridge).

4.4.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: JT SURVIVORSHIP vs WILL: If co-owners are JOINT TENANTS in equity and one dies, survivorship operates — the deceased's share does NOT pass under their will or intestacy. A bequest of 'my share of the house' by a JT is INEFFECTIVE. Only a TIC can pass their share by will.
SEVERANCE BY WILL: A joint tenancy CANNOT be severed by will — only inter vivos. Even a will purporting to leave the JT share is ineffective to sever; the survivor still takes all.

FOUR UNITIES: Joint tenancy requires ALL FOUR unities (PITT). If any unity is absent, it is a tenancy in common. The most commonly tested missing unity is TIME — if interests vest at different times, cannot be JT.

MAXIMUM TRUSTEES: The maximum number of LEGAL (not equitable) co-owners who can appear on the title is FOUR. If five people buy together, only the first four named hold the legal title; the fifth is a beneficiary only. The limitation is on legal trustees, NOT on the number of beneficial owners.

s.15 FACTORS — SECURED CREDITOR: The interests of a secured creditor of a beneficiary are one of the s.15 factors a court considers on a s.14 application — NOT one of the overriding factors. In BANKRUPTCY (s.335A IA 1986 applies, not s.15 TLATA), after 1 year the creditor's interest becomes paramount unless exceptional circumstances.

4.3.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: LAND CHARGES — SEARCH NAME MUST BE EXACT: A land charges search result is only valid if the search was made against the EXACT name of the estate owner as it appears in the conveyance. If the deed names 'Peter Smyth' but the search was against 'Peter Smith', the search is ineffective. If the incorrectly-named search returns 'no entries', the buyer CANNOT rely on it — the search must be repeated. CRITICAL: for registrable land charges, the doctrine of actual/constructive/imputed notice does NOT apply. Notice is completely irrelevant for land charges.

POSSESSORY TITLE — UPGRADING TIMELINE: Possessory title (registered or unregistered) for freehold can be upgraded to title absolute after 12 years of adverse possession or by producing evidence of title. If the title was registered as possessory 7 years ago, the buyer CANNOT yet upgrade — 5 more years are needed to reach the 12-year threshold. Advise the client of this delay, not that they must immediately upgrade.

D(ii) vs D(iii) LAND CHARGES — KEY DISTINCTION: Class D(ii) = RESTRICTIVE COVENANT made after 1925 between freehold owners. Class D(iii) = EQUITABLE EASEMENT or similar equitable right. A defective deed (e.g., incorrectly executed) does not create a legal easement but may create an equitable easement → must be protected as D(iii), not D(ii).

body: LAND CHARGES SEARCH — EXACT NAME MATTERS: A land charges search in unregistered title must be made against the EXACT name as it appears in the deed. A search against 'Peter Smith' when the deed reads 'Peter Smyth' is against the wrong name — the search is invalid and must be repeated. Imputed/actual/constructive notice only applies to equitable interests NOT capable of registration as land charges. See 4.3.3.2.

C(iv) vs D(ii) LAND CHARGES — DON'T CONFUSE: Class C(iv) = estate contract (contract to buy/sell land, option, right of pre-emption). Class D(ii) = post-1925 restrictive covenant. These are frequently confused in MCQs. A buyer who wants to protect a contract to purchase unregistered land registers a C(iv), not D(ii). See 4.3.3.2.

4.2.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: REGISTERED vs UNREGISTERED: Do not apply registered land rules to unregistered land and vice versa. Check whether land is registered FIRST. LCA 1972 land charges apply only to UNREGISTERED land — in registered land, interests are protected by notice/restriction/overriding interest.

VOID vs VOIDABLE: Unregistered land charge not registered = VOID against a purchaser of a legal estate for money/money's worth (not voidable — absolutely void). This is harsh but clear (Midland Bank v Green). Actual notice is IRRELEVANT to registration requirement under LCA 1972.

OVERRIDING INTERESTS — ACTUAL OCCUPATION: The person must be in actual occupation AT THE TIME OF DISPOSITION. Also, the interest must have been discoverable on reasonable inspection OR the purchaser had actual knowledge. A person temporarily absent (e.g. in hospital) may still be in actual occupation (Chhokar v Chhokar).

CLASS OF TITLE: Absolute title does NOT mean the title is perfect/undefeasible — it just means HMLR was satisfied. The register can still be altered for mistakes. Possessory title = HMLR cannot verify chain; absolute title = HMLR verified.

TRIGGER FOR REGISTRATION: A lease of exactly 7 years does NOT trigger compulsory first registration — only leases with MORE THAN 7 years remaining must be registered. Leases of 7 years or under take effect as overriding interests if the tenant is in actual occupation.

POSSESSORY TITLE UPGRADE — APPLY NOW IF TITLE AVAILABLE: Possessory title can be upgraded to absolute title at ANY TIME if the proprietor can now produce documentary evidence establishing a good title (LRA 2002 s.62). It is NOT the case that upgrading must wait a fixed period if good title documents are available. The buyer's solicitor should insist the seller applies to upgrade before exchange, specifying the basis for the application. See 4.2.4.4.

❌ TRAP FLK2 mock 04/08 Q1 (missed) — WHEN DOES LEGAL TITLE PASS? UNREGISTERED land: on COMPLETION. REGISTERED land: only on REGISTRATION — LRA 2002 s.27, a registrable disposition 'does not operate at law until the relevant registration requirements are met'. The distractor 'once the transfer is registered at HM Land Registry' is the REGISTERED-land answer served up on UNREGISTERED facts. Identify which system applies from the stem BEFORE reading the options.

❌ COROLLARY — 'completed the purchase last month' is a DEADLINE clue, not a title clue. It signals that the 2-month s.6/s.7 window is still open, so the buyer's legal title has not yet been defeated. It does NOT mean title is pending. Do not let a date in the stem pull you toward the registration answer.

4.1.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: POSITIVE COVENANTS IN FREEHOLD — THE RENT-CHARGE MECHANISM: The burden of a POSITIVE covenant does not run with freehold land, so a successor cannot be sued on it directly. The standard mechanism for making a positive obligation bite on freehold successors is a RENT-CHARGE, which is one of the five legal interests and confers a RIGHT OF ENTRY on the rent-charge owner in the event of default. The manual gives the classic example: payment for communal services (play area, park, shared facilities) on a freehold housing estate. 'Impossible to enforce against a successor' is therefore the WRONG answer — the rent-charge is the answer. See 4.1.6.3 and 4.5.3.

FIVE LEGAL INTERESTS — CLOSED LIST: If the interest in the stem is not a freehold, a leasehold, a mortgage, an easement, a rent-charge, a profit a prendre or a right of entry, it is EQUITABLE and nothing can make it legal. A restrictive covenant is the commonest distractor — it can never be a legal interest, however it was created.

DEED WITNESSING — A PARTY CANNOT WITNESS: Look for a stem in which the 'witness' is another party to the same deed, or was not physically present when the signatory signed. Attestation fails, the deed is invalid, and NO legal interest is created — but an equitable interest may still have arisen if the right has been exercised.

s 2 LP(MP)A 1989 — ORAL AGREEMENT FOR SALE: A conversation in which one party agrees to sell land to another for a price is NOT a valid contract for the sale of land, however clear the terms. Writing, all terms, and signature by the contracting parties are all required.

FOUR LEGAL OWNERS MAXIMUM: If FIVE people buy together, only the first FOUR named can hold the legal estate and appear on the proprietorship register. They hold on trust for all five. The cap applies to the LEGAL estate only — there is no cap on beneficial owners.

TREES AND PLANTS PASS WITH THE LAND: A seller is NOT entitled to dig up and take trees and plants — they form part of the land and the buyer takes them on completion. Contrast curtains, blinds and fitted carpets, which are chattels the seller may remove.

10.5.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: SUCCESS FEES POST-LASPO: Since LASPO 2012, success fees in CFAs are NO LONGER recoverable from the losing party in most civil cases. They are payable by the CLIENT from any damages recovered. This is a major trap — pre-2013 cases allowed recovery from opponent; post-LASPO they do not.

LEGAL AID — NOT WIDELY AVAILABLE: Post-LASPO, most civil cases do NOT qualify for legal aid. The most common civil legal aid matters are: domestic violence/abuse, cases involving risk to children, mental health detention, asylum/immigration. Standard contract disputes, personal injury (except clinical negligence in exceptional circumstances), and most family matters (without DV element) do NOT qualify.

CRIMINAL LEGAL AID — MAGISTRATES' COURT: Representation orders for magistrates' court are subject to MEANS AND MERITS tests. The interests of justice test (merits) considers: risk of custody/livelihood, complex law, language barrier, third party interests. NOT automatic.

ATE INSURANCE PREMIUMS: ATE premiums are generally NOT recoverable from the losing party post-LASPO (except clinical negligence cases where expert reports are needed). BTE insurance should always be checked first — client may already have cover.

10.4.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: GENERAL PROHIBITION — CRIMINAL OFFENCE: Breach of s.19 FSMA is a CRIMINAL OFFENCE (max 2 years' imprisonment/unlimited fine) AND renders agreements unenforceable. Do not confuse with civil consequences only.

SOLICITORS — PROFESSIONAL FIRMS EXEMPTION: Solicitors are NOT automatically authorised. They can rely on the professional firms (exempt) regime for incidental regulated activities — but the activity must be genuinely incidental and not separately remunerated. If solicitors want to conduct regulated activities as a main business, they must be FCA-authorised.

FINANCIAL PROMOTION: The financial promotion restriction (s.21) is broader than the general prohibition — it covers communications about investment activity, not just carrying on the activity. A solicitor who writes a letter recommending a specific investment to a client may breach s.21 if not authorised to approve promotions.

10.3.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: POCA OFFENCES — UNIVERSAL: ss.327-329 POCA apply to EVERYONE, not just the regulated sector. A solicitor commits s.328 if they continue to act on a transaction knowing it involves criminal property — even ordinary conveyancing.

TIPPING OFF vs PREJUDICING AN INVESTIGATION: Tipping off (s.333A) applies in the REGULATED SECTOR and requires the disclosure to be likely to PREJUDICE an investigation. A general discussion about money laundering law is NOT tipping off. Prejudicing investigation (s.342) applies more broadly.

AUTHORISED DISCLOSURE — TIMING: The 'consent' defence requires the SAR to be submitted BEFORE the prohibited act is carried out. If the act has already occurred, the authorised disclosure provides no defence to that past act (though it may be relevant mitigation).

NCA MORATORIUM PERIOD: After an SAR is submitted, the NCA has 7 working days to refuse consent. If NCA gives consent or does not respond within 7 days, the solicitor may proceed. If consent refused, further 31-day moratorium period applies.

10.2.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: DIRECT vs INDIRECT DISCRIMINATION: Direct = because of the characteristic itself (intent irrelevant; no justification possible for most characteristics). Indirect = neutral PCP that disproportionately disadvantages a group — CAN be justified (proportionate means of achieving legitimate aim).

DISABILITY — REASONABLE ADJUSTMENTS: The duty to make reasonable adjustments is ANTICIPATORY for service providers (must think ahead) and REACTIVE for employers (arises when specific disabled employee is known). Failure to adjust cannot be justified — it is a standalone duty.
MARRIAGE AND CIVIL PARTNERSHIP: Only applies in EMPLOYMENT context (s.8). Does NOT extend to provision of services etc. Most narrow protected characteristic in scope.

HARASSMENT — RELATED TO NOT BECAUSE OF: Harassment under s.26 occurs where conduct is 'related to' a protected characteristic — broader than 'because of'. Third-party harassment: employer liability was removed by EA 2010 (as originally enacted) and later legislative changes; check current position.
