body: STANDARD OF PROVISION: For a surviving spouse/civil partner: 'such financial provision as it would be reasonable in all the circumstances for a husband or wife to receive' — this is a HIGH standard (not merely maintenance). For all other applicants: 'such financial provision as it would be reasonable in all the circumstances for the applicant to receive for his maintenance'.

TIME LIMIT: A claim must be issued within 6 months of the grant of representation (Probate or Letters of Administration). The court can extend this time limit — but it will only do so if there is sufficient reason and the extension will not prejudice the estate or beneficiaries.

COURT CONSIDERATIONS (s.3): The court considers: financial resources and needs of the applicant and beneficiaries; obligations and responsibilities of the deceased; size of the estate; physical or mental disability of any applicant or beneficiary; any other relevant matter (nature and duration of relationship for cohabitants).

PROPERTY AVAILABLE FOR ORDERS: The court considers 'net estate' — all property that the deceased could have disposed of immediately before death. THIS INCLUDES: property subject to a joint tenancy severed at death by notional order under s.10; property the deceased gave away (donatio mortis causa caught by s.8-9); contracts to leave property (caught by s.11). This is BROADER than the estate passing under the will/intestacy.

ANTI-AVOIDANCE: Under s.10 and s.11, dispositions made with the intention of defeating an application can be set aside or treated as part of the estate. The applicant must show the deceased made the disposition with the intention of defeating a claim.

13.6.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: EXECUTOR'S YEAR: The PRs are not obliged to distribute the estate until 12 months after the death. A beneficiary cannot demand distribution during the executor's year. However, the PRs must act diligently — they can distribute sooner if the estate allows.

INSOLVENT ESTATES — ORDER OF PAYMENT (AEA 1925, s.34 + Schedule 1, Part II): Funeral, testamentary and administration expenses → preferential debts → ordinary unsecured debts. For a solvent estate, debts are paid from: (i) undisposed-of residue; (ii) residue; (iii) property specifically charged; (iv) general pecuniary legacies; (v) specific legacies.

ASSENT: A personal representative must execute an assent to transfer a specific asset to a beneficiary. For registered land, an AS1 (assent of whole title) or AS3 (part) is used. An assent must be in writing and signed by the PR. Once made, the PR cannot retract.

DEVASTAVIT: A PR who administers the estate improperly (paying the wrong debts, distributing to the wrong beneficiary, selling at an undervalue) is personally liable to creditors and beneficiaries. Creditors can follow assets that have been wrongly distributed into the hands of the recipient.

PROTECTION ON DISTRIBUTION — s.27 TA 1925: A PR who distributes the estate after advertising for claims (London Gazette + newspapers local to the deceased's home) and waiting two months is protected from liability to unknown creditors. The PR must still pay known claims.

APPROPRIATION: A PR may appropriate any part of the estate in or towards satisfaction of any share or interest in the estate, provided the appropriation is at a fair value and (for beneficiaries who are adult and sui juris) with their consent.

13.5.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: GRANTS OF REPRESENTATION: Probate: issued to executor(s) named in a valid will. Letters of Administration (with will annexed): issued where there is a will but no executor (died, refused to prove, etc.). Letters of Administration (intestacy): issued where there is no will. The grant must be obtained before the PRs can deal with estate assets (except in the case of settled land).

PROVING THE WILL — PROBATE REGISTRY: An originating application is made to the Probate Registry. An original will must be lodged. If the testator died after 1 January 2022, a Statement of Truth replaces the oath. A postal application is possible for straightforward estates.

RENUNCIATION: An executor who has not intermeddled in the estate can renounce probate — must do so in writing before accepting the grant. Once the executor has intermeddled (taken some act recognising the role), renunciation is no longer possible.

POWER RESERVED: An executor who does not wish to prove at this time can have power reserved — the grant issues to the acting executor(s) and the non-acting executor can prove at a later date if the need arises (e.g., if the proving executor dies).

FOREIGN GRANT: A foreign grant of representation has no automatic effect in England and Wales. A separate grant (resealing or a new grant) may be needed for English assets. Resealing of Commonwealth grants is possible under the Colonial Probates Act 1892.

THE PROBATE THRESHOLD: Banks and other institutions may release small amounts (up to their own threshold) without a grant. For most practical purposes, a grant is required for any significant assets (land, bank accounts above the threshold).

13.4.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: SPOUSE + ISSUE IS NOT THE WHOLE ESTATE: the surviving spouse/CP takes everything ONLY where there is NO issue. Where there IS issue they take personal chattels + the statutory legacy + ONE HALF of residue; the issue take the other half.
THE SPOUSE'S HALF IS ABSOLUTE: it is NOT a life interest. Any option offering a life interest in the residue is wrong.
STATUTORY LEGACY FIGURE AND DATE: £322,000 for deaths on or after 26 July 2023; £270,000 for deaths between 6 February 2020 and 25 July 2023. Check the DATE OF DEATH in the scenario before choosing.

PERSONAL CHATTELS ARE DEFINED NARROWLY: tangible moveable property, OTHER THAN money and OTHER THAN assets used for business purposes or held for investment purposes. A valuable painting bought as an investment is not a personal chattel.
28-DAY SURVIVORSHIP: the spouse/CP must survive the deceased by 28 days to inherit on intestacy — in EITHER instance, issue or no issue.

NO ISSUE MEANS THE SPOUSE BEATS EVERYONE: if there is no issue the spouse takes the whole estate REGARDLESS of surviving parents, brothers or sisters. The classic wrong answer splits it with the deceased's siblings or parents.

APPROPRIATION OF THE HOME IS A RIGHT, NOT A REQUEST: the surviving spouse can REQUIRE the PRs to appropriate the matrimonial home (or the deceased's interest as tenant in common) in partial or total satisfaction of their entitlement — and can still do so where the home is worth MORE, provided they pay EQUALITY MONEY to the estate.

EARLIER CLASSES EXCLUDE LATER ONES ENTIRELY: a whole-blood sibling excludes a half-blood sibling absolutely; the half-blood does not share. Within a class members take equally on reaching 18 or marrying earlier.
STATUTORY TRUSTS DO NOT APPLY TO PARENTS OR GRANDPARENTS: for every other class a predeceased member's issue take their share PER STIRPES. Parents and grandparents take equally with no substitution.

JOINT TENANCY PASSES BY SURVIVORSHIP: a beneficial JOINT TENANT'S interest does NOT pass under the will or intestacy. A TENANT IN COMMON'S share DOES. This is the most heavily tested distinction in the chapter.

PENSION NOMINATIONS ARE NON-BINDING: death benefits are usually held on DISCRETIONARY trusts and the member's nomination is a preference only — the trustees decide. But not all schemes work this way; some death-in-service benefits fall into the estate.

ADOPTED CHILDREN BELONG TO THE ADOPTIVE FAMILY: treated as children of their adoptive parents, NOT their natural parents, in both directions — they inherit on the adoptive family's intestacies and their own estate goes to the adoptive family.

UNMARRIED PARENTS — THE FATHER PRESUMPTION: the intestacy rules apply regardless of whether the parents were married, BUT where they never married the father is PRESUMED not to have survived the deceased — rebutted by evidence to the contrary OR by his being named on the birth certificate.
NOMINATED PROPERTY IS CAPPED: statutory nomination covers friendly societies, National Savings Bank and National Savings Certificates, and applies to deposits NOT EXCEEDING £5,000.

OUTSIDE THE ESTATE FOR SUCCESSION, INSIDE FOR IHT: jointly owned property, life interests in trust property and gifts with reservation of benefit DO form part of the estate for INHERITANCE TAX even though they are not payable to the PRs. Read whether the question asks about succession or tax.

13.3.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: EXECUTOR vs ADMINISTRATOR: An executor is appointed by the will and obtains a Grant of Probate. An administrator is appointed by the court (usually where there is no will or the executor cannot/will not act) and obtains Letters of Administration. An administrator WITH will annexed (donde non concessit) is appointed where there is a will but no acting executor.

SPECIFIC vs GENERAL vs DEMONSTRATIVE vs PECUNIARY LEGACIES: Specific: a particular identified item ('my Rolex watch'). General: a gift of a type not limited to a specific asset ('a car'). Demonstrative: a general legacy payable from a specific fund. Pecuniary: a sum of money. Specific legacies fail by ademption if the specific asset no longer exists at the testator's death.

ABATEMENT: If the estate is insufficient to pay all legacies in full, abatement occurs. Pecuniary and general legacies abate first (in proportion); then demonstrative legacies; then specific legacies. Residue bears the burden before other legacies.

LAPSE OF GIFTS: A gift lapses if the beneficiary predeceases the testator. The lapsed gift falls into residue (or if the residue itself lapses, intestacy). Exception — s.33 Wills Act 1837: a gift to a child or remoter issue of the testator that lapses because the child/issue predeceases the testator is saved IF that person left issue who survive the testator.

PRIVILEGED WILLS (SOLDIERS/MARINERS): A soldier on actual military service, a mariner or seaman at sea can make an informal will — oral or unwitnessed. No age requirement. The privilege continues for a reasonable period after active service ends.

CONSTRUCTION OF WILLS: If language in the will is ambiguous, the court applies various rules of construction: the armchair principle (standing in the testator's position knowing their circumstances); admissible extrinsic evidence to resolve a latent ambiguity.

13.2.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: POST-EXECUTION ALTERATIONS ARE INEFFECTIVE UNLESS EXECUTED IN THE MARGIN: inserting words, crossing them out, or both, will NOT work after execution. The amendment must ITSELF be formally executed IN THE MARGIN of the page near the relevant amendment — or the will confirmed by a CODICIL.

THE OBLITERATION EXCEPTION IS ABOUT LEGIBILITY, NOT INTENTION: where the obliteration is SO COMPLETE that the original words are NO LONGER APPARENT, those words are treated as REVOKED even though the obliteration was never executed. The result is a gift of NOTHING — not a reversion to the original figure.

MAGNIFYING GLASS ONLY: a magnifying glass may be used to test whether the original words are apparent. The use of OTHER TECHNIQUES IS NOT PERMITTED. An option relying on infra-red or forensic imaging is wrong.

PRE-EXECUTION ALTERATIONS ARE VALID IN PRINCIPLE BUT PRESUMED OTHERWISE: they are in principle valid regardless of separate execution — BUT the court ASSUMES they were made AFTER execution and are therefore INVALID, unless separately executed or there is other evidence, such as an attending witness or an attendance note.

A CODICIL REPUBLISHES THE WILL: if the will was altered before republication and the alteration is unexecuted, republication CAN validate it. But there is then a presumption that the unexecuted alteration was made AFTER execution of the CODICIL, and evidence is required to rebut that.

FOUR METHODS OF REVOCATION, AND ONLY THREE ARE DELIBERATE: subsequent will; destruction; obliteration or alteration; and marriage or civil partnership. Marriage is the one testators often do not realise revokes their will.

A LATER WILL DOES NOT AUTOMATICALLY REVOKE AN EARLIER ONE: it revokes the prior will ONLY INSOFAR AS IT IS INCONSISTENT. Where a testator has more than one will, provisions that can be read CONSISTENTLY with each other all take effect. That is why a revocation clause is standard practice.

THE REVOCATION CLAUSE CAN GO TOO FAR: care must be taken NOT to include a general clause revoking all previous wills where the testator has other wills covering specific assets or specific COUNTRIES that they do not wish to revoke.

DESTRUCTION NEEDS BOTH ACT AND INTENTION: burning, tearing or otherwise destroying, by the testator OR by someone else at the testator's DIRECTION AND IN THEIR PRESENCE, WITH the intention of revoking. DESTRUCTION ALONE WILL NOT REVOKE.
CROSSING OUT OR WRITING 'CANCELLED' IS NOT DESTRUCTION: neither amounts to burning, tearing or otherwise destroying the will.

TWO REBUTTABLE PRESUMPTIONS TO LEARN: a will found MUTILATED at the date of death is presumed to have been mutilated by the testator with intent to revoke; and a will last known to have been IN THE TESTATOR'S POSSESSION but which CANNOT BE FOUND at death is presumed destroyed by the testator with intent to revoke. Both are REBUTTABLE.

DEPENDENT RELATIVE REVOCATION IS RARE AND CONDITIONAL: it applies where the intention to revoke was CONDITIONAL on a future event, such as executing a new will. If that event did not happen, the original will may still be valid EVEN IF DESTROYED — provided it can be RECONSTRUCTED FROM A COPY OR DRAFT.

MARRIAGE REVOKES COMPLETELY; DIVORCE ONLY PARTLY: subsequent marriage or civil partnership COMPLETELY revokes the will unless it appears from the will that the testator expected to marry a PARTICULAR PERSON and intended it not to be revoked. Divorce, dissolution or annulment revokes only PARTLY — the remainder of the will remains valid.

ON DIVORCE THE EX IS TREATED AS HAVING DIED ON THE DATE OF THE ORDER: so their appointment as executor or trustee is ineffective, gifts to them are revoked, and any SUBSTITUTIONAL provisions drafted to take effect if they had predeceased the testator ARE ENGAGED. It takes a FINAL ORDER of divorce.
SEPARATION DOES NOTHING: the divorce provisions do NOT apply on separation. And divorce will not amend a will where a CONTRARY INTENTION is stated in it.

MUTUAL WILLS ARE A CONTRACT PLUS A CONSTRUCTIVE TRUST: wills made by two or more persons, usually with the same clauses and conferring reciprocal benefits, further to an AGREEMENT to make such wills and NOT TO REVOKE without the other's consent. That agreement creates a CONTRACT that the wills are to be irrevocable and remain unaltered; it is an EQUITABLE principle creating a CONSTRUCTIVE TRUST in favour of the beneficiaries.

body: ATTESTATION CLAUSE: An attestation clause creates a REBUTTABLE presumption of due execution (that the formal requirements were met). Without an attestation clause, the Probate Registry will require an affidavit from a witness (or other satisfactory evidence).

WITNESSES CANNOT BENEFIT: A beneficiary (or spouse/civil partner of a beneficiary) who witnesses the will cannot take their gift under the will (s.15 Wills Act 1837). The witness and their spouse can take NOTHING — not even on intestacy under the will.

body: KNOWLEDGE AND APPROVAL: The testator must know and approve of the contents of the will. Suspicious circumstances (e.g., the will was prepared by a beneficiary) shift the burden to the propounder to prove knowledge and approval.

UNDUE INFLUENCE (WILLS): Unlike in contract, undue influence in wills is NEVER presumed — it must be PROVED by those alleging it. The standard is high: the influence must be coercive (overbearing the testator's own volition).

6.5.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: FOLLOWING vs TRACING: Following tracks the asset itself as it moves. Tracing is the process of identifying a new asset as the substitute for the old one. Tracing in equity is available against a fiduciary even into mixed funds.

LOWEST INTERMEDIATE BALANCE RULE: Where a trustee mixes trust money with their own and makes withdrawals, the trust can only trace into what remains up to the lowest balance the account reached after mixing — the trustee is assumed to spend their own money first (Roscoe v Winder — only if the trustee intended to replenish).

BACKWARD TRACING: Foskett v McKeown [2001] — equitable tracing follows the proceeds even where payment precedes the breach if there was a coordinated scheme (the debt must be discharged by the later misappropriation).

KNOWING RECEIPT vs KNOWING ASSISTANCE: Knowing receipt (s.29 Trustee Act — personal liability): Recipient must receive trust property for their own benefit AND have knowledge (actual, Nelsonian or constructive) that it was trust property. Knowing assistance (Barnes v Addy — also called 'dishonest assistance'): requires DISHONESTY — Baden v Société Générale knowledge types 1-5, but Royal Brunei Airlines v Tan requires objective dishonesty.

CHANGE OF POSITION DEFENCE: A defendant who has received trust money in good faith and has changed their position in reliance on it (spent money they would not otherwise have spent) has a defence to the extent of that change.

PROPRIETARY vs PERSONAL CLAIMS: A proprietary claim (to the specific asset or its substitute) has priority in insolvency. A personal claim (for the value of the loss) is unsecured and ranks with general creditors. Always prefer a proprietary claim if the asset can be traced.

6.4.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: NO-CONFLICT vs NO-PROFIT — DISTINCT RULES: No-conflict = cannot place self in position of actual or potential conflict between duty and personal interest (e.g., self-dealing). No-profit = cannot make any personal profit from the position, even without conflict and even without beneficiary loss. Both rules are strict. A trustee can breach the no-profit rule without any conflict of interest.

SELF-DEALING vs FAIR DEALING: Self-dealing (trustee buys trust property) = voidable at ANY beneficiary's request regardless of whether the price is fair. Fair dealing (trustee buys a beneficiary's beneficial interest) = valid only IF trustee proves: (a) no advantage taken of position; (b) full disclosure to beneficiary; (c) transaction fair and honest. Confusing which rule applies is a common MCQ error.

NO-PROFIT IS STRICT: Liability does not require bad faith. Profit made using information or an opportunity acquired through the trusteeship must be accounted for even if beneficiaries suffered no loss and even if information was in the public domain (Boardman v Phipps). The key question is whether the profit arose because of the fiduciary position.

REMUNERATION — TRUSTEES NOT AUTOMATICALLY PAID: Trustees accept office without expectation of payment. Remuneration is only permitted if: (a) trust deed contains a charging clause; (b) beneficiaries (sui juris) authorise it with full disclosure; (c) court authorises under inherent jurisdiction; or (d) TA 2000 s.29 (professional trustee, no express charging clause). Expenses (not profit) are reimbursable: TA 2000 s.31(1).

DUTY OF CARE — PROFESSIONAL STANDARD: The standard of care rises for professional trustees — judged by the skill they hold themselves out as having (TA 2000 s.1(b)). Statutory duty of care applies to investment, delegation, etc. but NOT to dispositive powers (deciding who receives trust property).

COWAN v SCARGILL — ETHICAL INVESTING: Trustees CANNOT block or restrict investments on moral/political grounds if doing so would harm financial returns for beneficiaries. Ethical considerations are only permissible where: (a) two investments offer the same financial return, or (b) ethical investment is consistent with the trust's purposes (Harries v Church Commissioners — charities). Private trusts: financial interests are paramount.

ADVANCEMENT — FULL SHARE SINCE TA 2000: Before the TA 2000 amendments, trustees could advance only up to 50% of a beneficiary's share (TA 1925 s.32 original). Post-TA 2000, trustees may advance up to the WHOLE presumptive share. The amount advanced is deducted from the beneficiary's final entitlement. Where there is a life tenant, their consent is required as capital removal affects income.

DELEGATION — WHAT CANNOT BE DELEGATED (TA 2000 s.11): Trustees CANNOT delegate: (a) any function relating to distribution of assets; (b) decisions on whether payments come from income or capital; (c) power to appoint trustees; (d) any other function excluded by statute or trust instrument. Investment management and administrative functions CAN be delegated. Delegation must be in writing (s.15). Beneficiaries cannot be appointed agents (s.12(3)).

6.3.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps - Common Errors
body: CY-PRES TIMING: initial failure needs GENERAL charitable intention (specific intention = resulting trust to donor); subsequent failure is AUTOMATIC. Amalgamation is no failure at all (Re Faraker).

PERSONAL NEXUS + POVERTY EXCEPTION: employer/ancestor classes fail public benefit (Oppenheim) EXCEPT under relief of poverty. Charging fees does not defeat charitable status if the poor are not excluded.
ANOMALOUS PURPOSE TRUSTS: closed list (Re Endacott) - a novel-sounding purpose is not covered. 21-year cap + willing trustee. Fox hunting is a classic distractor: now INVALID (Hunting Act 2004).
UNINCORPORATED ASSOCIATIONS: outright gift on the members' CONTRACTUAL rules, not a purpose trust.

RT vs CICT: purchase money resulting trust governs COMMERCIAL property; CICT governs the DOMESTIC home (Jones v Kernott). Deposit/initial contribution = RT; SUBSEQUENT mortgage payments = constructive trust.

'SHARE THE HOME' MEANS OWNERSHIP, NOT COHABITATION: 'let's share a family home' and 'this will benefit us both' INSUFFICIENT; 'everything's 50:50' and 'half yours' SUFFICIENT. Stems quote these near-verbatim.
JOINT NAMES: unequal contributions do NOT automatically mean unequal shares (Fowler v Barron). Rebuttal needs alternative intention at purchase, or a varied intention later.
DETRIMENTAL RELIANCE is a SEPARATE hurdle for an EXPRESS CICT, but almost automatic for an INFERRED one.
ADVANCEMENT IS RELATIONSHIP-SPECIFIC: father-child and man-wife/fiancee. NOT generally mother-child (Laskar).
UNCONSCIONABILITY is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT in estoppel (Cobbe) - and the remedy is the MINIMUM equity, not automatically what was promised.

ASSISTANCE vs RECEIPT: assistance turns on the THIRD PARTY'S DISHONESTY (trustee's honesty irrelevant); receipt turns on UNCONSCIONABILITY and requires BENEFICIAL receipt - a mere conduit is not liable under that head.
Both are PERSONAL claims and only arise where a proprietary remedy will not work - no double restitution. Proprietary claims need the asset or traceable proceeds (see 6.5).

body.head: SAUNDERS v VAUTIER — ALL BENEFICIARIES MUST BE ADULT AND ABSOLUTELY ENTITLED: The rule allows beneficiaries to call in the trust and do as they wish with the property — but ONLY if ALL beneficiaries are

body: SAUNDERS v VAUTIER — ALL THREE REQUIREMENTS: To collapse a trust, ALL beneficiaries must be: (1) ADULT (18+), (2) sui juris (no incapacity), AND (3) together absolutely entitled to the ENTIRE trust property. ONE minor beneficiary or ONE potential unborn beneficiary defeats the rule. See 6.2.3.

DISCRETIONARY TRUST — NO COMPLETE LIST REQUIRED (UNLIKE FIXED): Trustees of a discretionary trust do NOT need to produce a complete list of all potential beneficiaries. The 'any given postulant' test suffices. BUT a life tenant MUST consent to any modification of the trust affecting their interest. See 6.2.2.1 and 6.2.2.2.

6.1.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: TANGIBLES v INTANGIBLES — SEGREGATION: tangibles must be separated from the bulk — 20 bottles from a cellar of 200 identical bottles is UNCERTAIN unless segregated (Re London Wine Co; Re Goldcorp Exchange). Intangibles of equal value (same-class shares) need NO segregation (Hunter v Moss). Identical goods sitting in a warehouse = no trust.

SUBJECT MATTER — CERTAIN v UNCERTAIN WORDING: CERTAIN = 'the residue of my estate' (Sprange v Barnard); 'reasonable income' where objectively determinable (Re Golay's Will Trusts); a stated number of identical shares; a nominal opening sum with assets added later. UNCERTAIN = 'some of my shares'; 'the bulk of my estate'; an unidentified part of a collection (Boyce v Boyce).

'FRIENDS' IS CONCEPTUALLY UNCERTAIN: a trust for 'my friends' is likely to FAIL — 'friend' cannot be defined with sufficient certainty (Re Barlow's Will Trusts). 'My nieces and nephews' is likely to SUCCEED if they can be identified.

INTENTION MISSING DOES NOT MEAN NOTHING HAPPENS: no certainty of intention (and subject matter certain) = the recipient takes an OUTRIGHT GIFT for their own benefit. Only UNCERTAIN OBJECTS produce a resulting trust; only UNCERTAIN SUBJECT MATTER produces a void trust.

CONSTITUTION OF SHARES — SIGNING THE FORM IS NOT ENOUGH: (1) sign the stock transfer form AND (2) send it with the share certificates to the company registrar. Legal title passes on REGISTRATION. Re Rose rescues it only once the settlor has done ALL in their power — not a form still in a drawer.

s 53(1)(b) v s 53(1)(c): (b) trust of LAND = evidenced in writing — the oral declaration is VALID immediately but UNENFORCEABLE until written evidence exists. (c) disposition of a SUBSISTING EQUITABLE interest = must BE in writing — a VALIDITY requirement, and a later document is generally too late.

DISCRETIONARY TRUSTEES CANNOT GO OUTSIDE THE CLASS: trustees select freely within the class and need give no reasons, but may NOT benefit someone outside it unless the instrument authorises extending the class.
A TRUST CANNOT BE SET UP FOR AN UNBORN CHILD, but a trust can be settled once the child is born, with defined future children joining the class as they are born.

1.5.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors

body.head: REMOTENESS - THE TWO LIMBS
items: NORMAL loss - arises naturally, according to the usual course of things. Inevitably within reasonable contemplation.
ABNORMAL loss - within contemplation ONLY if the special circumstances were known to BOTH parties AT THE TIME OF THE CONTRACT. Knowledge acquired later, or at the date of breach, is TOO LATE.

body: PENALTY v LIQUIDATED DAMAGES: the test is NOT simply “genuine pre-estimate”. Ask whether the detriment imposed is PROPORTIONATE to a LEGITIMATE INTEREST the innocent party is protecting. There is NO legitimate interest in merely punishing the defaulter.
PENALTY CONSEQUENCE: the clause is struck out and IGNORED - the claim is not lost. C falls back on UNLIQUIDATED damages.
MITIGATION - BURDEN OF PROOF: on the DEFENDANT to show C failed to take reasonable steps. Not on C to prove they mitigated.
ANTICIPATORY BREACH: the duty to mitigate arises only where C ACCEPTS the breach. C who does NOT accept has NO duty to mitigate.
EXPECTATION v RELIANCE: reliance CANNOT be used to escape a BAD BARGAIN - that would put C in a better position than performance = unjust enrichment.

THIRD PARTY LOSS: usually NOMINAL damages only - C recovers their own loss, not another's. Family holiday booking is the recognised exception (own disappointment PLUS disappointment at the family's disappointment).

NON-PECUNIARY LOSS: damages for disappointment or injured feelings are NOT usually recoverable. Exception where the very object of the contract was a happy/pleasurable experience or greater peace of mind.

EQUITABLE REMEDIES ARE NEVER AS OF RIGHT: specific performance refused where damages are adequate, and NEVER granted for a contract of employment. It CAN however be granted for a third party's benefit.
CONTRIBUTORY NEGLIGENCE: reduces contract damages only where liability is CONCURRENT in tort. Breach of a strict contractual duty alone → no reduction (Law Reform (Contributory Negligence) Act 1945).
GUARANTEE FORMALITY: a contract of guarantee must be EVIDENCED IN WRITING - s IV Statute of Frauds 1677. An indemnity needs no such formality. Distinguish the two.

1.4.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: SUBSTANTIAL vs PARTIAL PERFORMANCE: the single most-tested distinction. SUBSTANTIAL = innocent party must pay, less a deduction (damages for breach of warranty). PARTIAL = performer recovers NOTHING unless the injured party accepts it. Be aware of a situation where apparent 'substantial' performance is really partial.
PARTIAL PERFORMANCE NEEDS A GENUINE CHOICE: quantum meruit only arises where the injured party had a real option to accept OR reject. Forced acceptance is not acceptance.

LATE PERFORMANCE IS GOOD PERFORMANCE unless TIME IS OF THE ESSENCE. Without that, the remedy is damages only — no right to repudiate. Watch for the third route in: a party subjected to unreasonable delay can SERVE NOTICE making time of the essence.

DISCHARGE BY AGREEMENT NEEDS CONSIDERATION unless executed BY DEED — including for a WAIVER of a term. Unilateral discharge is accord and satisfaction: accord = the agreement, satisfaction = the consideration.

ANTICIPATORY BREACH — IF YOU AFFIRM, YOU MUST KEEP PERFORMING. Refusing to accept the repudiation and waiting for the due date obliges the innocent party to continue performing its own obligations, and the defaulter may rectify the breach and continue the contract.

AFFIRMATION — NO DUTY TO MITIGATE: where the innocent party validly elects to continue, it may do so however unreasonable that seems. Two limits: performance must not require the other side's CO-OPERATION, and the party must have a LEGITIMATE INTEREST beyond claiming damages.

DAMAGES ALWAYS; REPUDIATION SOMETIMES: every breach gives a right to damages. Only breach of a CONDITION, or of an INTERMEDIATE term with serious consequences, or repudiation/fundamental breach, allows the innocent party to treat the contract as discharged.

SELF-INDUCED FRUSTRATION IS NO FRUSTRATION. Also NOT frustration: performance merely more expensive or more difficult; and a case where the contract itself gives scope for an alternative method of performance, or an alternative exists that is not fundamentally different in COMMERCIAL terms.
FRUSTRATION RELEASES FUTURE OBLIGATIONS ONLY. Obligations already existing at the moment of frustration must still be performed.

COMMON LAW RECOVERY IS WORSE THAN THE ACT: at common law, advance payments may be recovered BUT if any benefit had been received under the transaction, no monies paid can be recovered; and on destruction of the subject matter there is no right to expenses. It is better to claim under the LRFCA 1943.

THE 1943 ACT DOES NOT COVER EVERYTHING: excluded are carriage of goods by sea and charterparties, insurance, and the sale of specific goods that have perished. ASSESSMENT TIP — be wary of a scenario involving a contract ostensibly frustrated by DELAYS AT SEA.

COMMON MISTAKE vs FRUSTRATION (boundary trap, see 1.3): common mistake concerns a state of affairs at the moment of FORMATION; frustration concerns a SUPERVENING event after formation that was not the fault of either party. Vitiating factors are covered in 1.3, not here.

1.3.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: MISREPRESENTATION DAMAGES — CONTRACT vs TORT MEASURE: Where a misrepresentation has been incorporated as a contractual WARRANTY, damages = EXPECTATION (contract) measure = put claimant in the position as if the representation were true = (value as represented) − (actual value). Distinguish from the tortious measure for non-contractual misrepresentation = (purchase price) − (actual value). In the painting example: represented value £20,000 − actual value £150 = £19,850.

LIMITATION — DATE OF BREACH NOT DISCOVERY: For breach of contract, the 6-year limitation period runs from the DATE THE BREACH OCCURRED, not from when the claimant discovered the breach. Discovery only delays time in limited contexts (fraud, concealment). A buyer who discovers wrong goods years later can still claim if the breach was less than 6 years ago.

DURESS TO PROPERTY — VOIDABLE + TIME BAR: A threat to damage property (even sentimental property) = duress. Contract is VOIDABLE (not void); remedy = rescission. But rescission may be barred by lapse of time, affirmation, or third-party rights. Always consider whether the time to rescind has passed. See 1.3.5.1.

1.2.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: UNLABELLED / INNOMINATE TERMS: A clause without an express label (not stated as 'condition' or 'warranty') is classified as an innominate term. The remedy depends on the CONSEQUENCES of breach — if consequences are trivial, only damages; if substantial (i.e., party deprived of substantially the whole benefit), treated as condition → right to terminate. Substantial performance of an innominate term still entitles the performing party to payment (less a deduction for the breach).

INNOMINATE TERMS — CONSEQUENCE NOT LABEL: For an innominate term, the remedy depends on the CONSEQUENCE of the breach (was the innocent party deprived of substantially the whole benefit?), not the label. Insubstantial consequence = damages only, not termination. A party who receives some benefit cannot refuse all payment. See 1.2.7.

1.1.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: COUSINS / COMMERCIAL CONTEXT: do not apply the domestic/social presumption (no ITCLR) between cousins or other family members where the transaction has a COMMERCIAL CHARACTER — a loan for a business, financial gain. The commercial presumption applies once money and business are involved.

CERTAINTY — PRICE AS 'GOING RATE': a contract is NOT void for uncertainty on price merely because the exact sum is unspecified. 'The going rate', 'market price' or 'reasonable price' each provide a sufficiently certain MECHANISM. Void only if price is wholly absent AND no mechanism exists.

CERTAINTY — QUALITY TERMS: a quality descriptor ('most optimum', 'best quality') does not make a contract void for uncertainty — the court will imply a reasonable-quality standard. Distinguish a genuinely MEANINGLESS term.

PROMISSORY ESTOPPEL — DETRIMENTAL RELIANCE: where a promisor acts in reliance on a promise to accept less (e.g. buys extra materials), estoppel prevents the promisee going back to the full amount. The promise must be CLEAR AND UNEQUIVOCAL and there must be an ALTERATION OF POSITION in reliance — see the five-element grid above. SHIELD NOT SWORD: it is a defence, never a cause of action.
COUNTER-OFFER KILLS THE OFFER; A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION DOES NOT. 'Would you take cash or a bank transfer?' is a request for information — the original offer survives.
THE POSTAL RULE STILL BITES WHEN THE LETTER NEVER ARRIVES, provided it was correctly addressed and posted in a post box. But it is DISPLACED by a requirement of 'NOTICE IN WRITING'.

REVOCATION NEED NOT COME FROM THE OFFEROR: a reliable THIRD PARTY can communicate it. And an offer stated to be open until a date CAN still be revoked before then — unless it is a UNILATERAL offer and the offeree HAS STARTED PERFORMANCE, in which case it cannot be revoked at all.
DEATH CUTS BOTH WAYS DIFFERENTLY: the OFFEREE'S death ends the offer outright. The OFFEROR'S death does NOT necessarily — an offeree IGNORANT of the death can still accept.
SUFFICIENT, NOT ADEQUATE: consideration needs SOME value and must be legal; it need not be a fair price. £1 annual rent plus a promise to keep the property in good order is sufficient.

PART PAYMENT ON THE DUE DATE DOES NOT DISCHARGE THE DEBT — three exceptions only: a chattel instead of money, a smaller sum EARLIER, or a smaller sum at a DIFFERENT PLACE. And a JUDGMENT debt carries interest, which must also be cleared.

EXISTING DUTY — WHO IT IS OWED TO DECIDES IT: a duty owed to a THIRD PARTY is good consideration; an existing PUBLIC duty or duty imposed by law is not, unless exceeded; an existing CONTRACTUAL duty is not, unless performance became SUBSTANTIALLY DIFFERENT.
SEPARATION IS NOT ENOUGH to rebut the social/domestic presumption between spouses or civil partners — DIVORCE OR DISSOLUTION is.

WRITING vs EVIDENCED IN WRITING: LAND contracts must BE IN WRITING (LP(MP)A 1989 s 2). GUARANTEES need only be EVIDENCED in writing — a note or memo covering all material terms, under the Statute of Frauds 1677 s IV. Land falls into BOTH categories.

MINORS AND NECESSARIES: valid and binding only IF FOR THE MINOR'S BENEFIT. Otherwise not binding unless RATIFIED on reaching majority. Necessaries extend beyond bare essentials and are a QUESTION OF FACT turning on the minor's condition in life at the time of SALE AND DELIVERY.
C(RTP)A 1999 IS ONE-WAY: a third party can ENFORCE a term benefiting them where they are IDENTIFIED (s 1(3)). It never allows a contract to be enforced AGAINST a third party.

7.20.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: IHT THRESHOLDS 2024/25: Nil-rate band (NRB): £325,000 (frozen until 2030). Residence Nil-Rate Band (RNRB): £175,000 where a qualifying residential property is left to direct descendants. Unused NRB and RNRB can be transferred to surviving spouse/civil partner (up to 100%).

BUSINESS RELIEF (BR) (formerly Business Property Relief/BPR): 100% relief for unincorporated businesses, interests in an unincorporated business, and unquoted (AIM) shares. 50% relief for controlling shareholding in a quoted company and certain business assets used by the business. The asset must have been owned for at least 2 years.

POTENTIALLY EXEMPT TRANSFERS (PETs): A lifetime gift to an individual (or certain trusts) is a PET — no IHT if the donor survives 7 years. If the donor dies within 7 years, taper relief reduces the tax owed: 3-4 years: 20% reduction; 4-5: 40%; 5-6: 60%; 6-7: 80%. The tax on the PET is charged at the rates applicable at death.

CHARGEABLE LIFETIME TRANSFERS (CLTs): Gifts to discretionary trusts etc. are immediately chargeable at the lifetime rate of 20% (50% of the death rate). If the donor dies within 7 years, an additional 20% may be due (or taper relief applies).

ANNUAL EXEMPTION: £3,000 per tax year. Unused annual exemption can be carried forward ONE year only (not accumulated beyond that). Small gifts exemption: £250 per donee per year (cannot combine with annual exemption for the same donee).

QUICK SUCCESSION RELIEF (QSR): If a person inherits property that has already been subject to IHT within the last 5 years, relief reduces the IHT on the second death. The relief decreases over time: 100% within 1 year, 80% 1-2 years, 60% 2-3, 40% 3-4, 20% 4-5.

7.19.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: VAT REGISTRATION THRESHOLD 2024/25: £90,000. Registration is compulsory once taxable supplies in any 12-month rolling period exceed this. Must notify HMRC within 30 days of the end of the month in which the threshold was exceeded.

TAXABLE SUPPLIES vs EXEMPT SUPPLIES: Standard-rated (20%), reduced-rated (5%) and zero-rated supplies are all 'taxable' — the trader can recover input tax. EXEMPT supplies: the trader cannot recover input tax attributable to those supplies. Partial exemption rules apply if both taxable and exempt supplies are made.

ZERO-RATED vs EXEMPT: Zero-rated goods (e.g. food, children's clothes, books) are taxed at 0% — the supplier can reclaim input VAT. Exempt supplies (e.g. insurance, financial services, most residential lettings): the supplier cannot reclaim input VAT. This distinction is heavily tested.

OPTION TO TAX (COMMERCIAL PROPERTY): Commercial property transactions are normally exempt. But a VAT-registered person can opt to tax a commercial property, making the supply standard-rated. Once opted, all future supplies of that property are standard-rated (unless the option is revoked within 6 months or after 20 years).

VAT ON LAND AND PROPERTY: Sale/lease of residential property: zero-rated (new build) or exempt (resale). Sale of commercial property: exempt UNLESS the seller has opted to tax. Building works: zero-rated for new residential construction; standard-rated for commercial construction and renovations.

TIME AND AMOUNT OF SUPPLY — TAX POINT: Basic tax point = when goods are removed or services performed. Actual tax point overrides if an invoice is issued or payment received within 14 days before or after the basic tax point (14-day rule). Getting the tax point wrong causes the return to be wrong.

7.18.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: CGT ANNUAL EXEMPT AMOUNT 2024/25: £3,000. Unused allowance CANNOT be carried forward to another year. The allowance is deducted from net chargeable gains (after losses) in the year.

CGT RATES 2024/25: Basic rate taxpayers: 10% on assets (18% on residential property and carried interest). Higher/additional rate: 20% (24% on residential property). The rate depends on whether the taxpayer's total income + gains exceeds the basic rate band.

BUSINESS ASSET DISPOSAL RELIEF (BADR): 10% tax on qualifying gains up to the £1 million lifetime limit. Qualifying conditions: must hold the shares in a trading company for at least 2 years; must be an employee/officer; must hold at least 5% of ordinary share capital and voting rights. Does NOT apply to investment companies.

CHATTELS EXEMPTION: An asset with a predictable useful life of ≤50 years is a wasting chattel and is exempt from CGT. A non-wasting chattel sold for £6,000 or less is also exempt (small chattels exemption). Gain on a non-wasting chattel sold for more than £6,000 is capped at 5/3 × (proceeds − £6,000).

PRINCIPAL PRIVATE RESIDENCE RELIEF (PPR): Exempts the gain attributable to periods of actual or deemed occupation. The final 9 months of ownership always qualifies (even if not in occupation). Lettings relief has been substantially restricted.

NO CGT ON DEATH — 'FREE UPLIFT': Assets passing on death are treated as acquired by the beneficiary at market value at the date of death. No CGT on the death itself. A legatee's base cost = market value at death.

7.17.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: CORPORATION TAX RATES 2023/24 ONWARDS: Main rate 25% for companies with profits over £250,000. Small profits rate 19% for profits up to £50,000. Marginal relief applies between £50,000 and £250,000. For associated companies, the thresholds are divided by the number of associated companies.

CORPORATION TAX — ACCOUNTING PERIOD: Usually 12 months; broadly follows the company's accounting period. CT600 return due 12 months after the end of the accounting period. Tax payment: large companies pay by quarterly instalments; others pay 9 months after the end of the accounting period.

LOAN RELATIONSHIPS: Interest received is taxed as income; interest paid is a deductible expense. Only on an accruals basis for trading companies. Loans between connected companies: must use arm's-length pricing (transfer pricing).

GROUPS: Group relief allows trading losses to be surrendered from one group company to another (75% group). Capital gains can be rolled over across group companies. Gains on intra-group asset transfers are deferred (no-gain-no-loss transfer).

RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT RELIEF: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) can claim an enhanced deduction or (if loss-making) surrender losses for a tax credit. Large companies use the R&D expenditure credit (RDEC) system.

CHARGEABLE ACCOUNTING PERIODS: If a company changes its accounting date, there may be a short accounting period (under 12 months). If over 12 months, the HMRC splits into two: first 12 months + remainder.

7.16.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: INCOME TAX RATES 2024/25: Personal allowance £12,570; Basic rate 20% (£12,571–£50,270); Higher rate 40% (£50,271–£125,140); Additional rate 45% (above £125,140). The personal allowance is tapered at £1 for every £2 of income above £100,000 — it is fully withdrawn at £125,140.

SAVINGS AND DIVIDEND INCOME: Savings allowance: basic rate taxpayer £1,000; higher rate £500; additional rate £0. Dividend allowance: £500 (2024/25). Dividend rates: basic 8.75%, higher 33.75%, additional 39.35%. Savings income is taxed after non-savings income.
TRADING INCOME: Basis period reform (FA 2022): from 2024/25, all traders are taxed on profits arising in the tax year (not the accounting year ending in the tax year). Transitional provisions apply.

EMPLOYMENT INCOME: Benefits in kind taxed on the employee. Employer pays Class 1A NIC on benefits in kind. Company cars and fuel: taxed by reference to the list price x appropriate percentage (based on CO2 emissions).

RELIEF FOR LOSSES: Trading losses can be set against other income of the same or previous year, or carried forward against future trading profits of the same trade. Loss relief must be CLAIMED — it is not automatic.

SELF-ASSESSMENT AND PAYMENT: Tax return: 31 October (paper) / 31 January (online) following the tax year. Payment on account: two payments (31 January and 31 July) each = 50% of prior year's liability. Balancing payment: 31 January following the tax year.

7.15.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: BANKRUPTCY THRESHOLD: Creditor petition requires a debt of AT LEAST £5,000 (single creditor or combined). Debtor can petition for their own bankruptcy on any amount. A statutory demand for ≥£5,000 left unpaid for 21 days is evidence of inability to pay debts.

BANKRUPT'S ESTATE (s.283 IA 1986): Vests in trustee in bankruptcy. Includes ALL property belonging to the bankrupt at the date of the bankruptcy order (and after-acquired property). EXCLUDED: tools of the trade; clothing and basic household goods; property held on trust for others. Exempt: pension rights (generally protected).

BANKRUPT'S HOME: Trustee has 3 years to deal with interest in the family home. After 3 years, if trustee has not obtained a possession order or charging order, the interest re-vests in the bankrupt (s.283A IA 1986).

DISCHARGE: Automatic after 12 months from bankruptcy order (usually). Court can annul, suspend, or extend (e.g. for failure to cooperate). During bankruptcy: restrictions on obtaining credit (>£500 without disclosing bankruptcy); cannot be a company director; cannot act as an IP.

IVA vs BANKRUPTCY: IVA is a VOLUNTARY arrangement — requires 75% in value of creditors. Once approved, binds ALL creditors including dissenting ones. Trustee/supervisor is an IP. Key advantage: no automatic restrictions; no public stigma of bankruptcy; business can continue.

CLAW-BACK (individual): Same concepts apply as in corporate insolvency — transaction at undervalue (s.339 IA 1986) and preferences (s.340 IA 1986). Look-back: 5 years (undervalue if associate); 2 years (other undervalue); 6 months (preference non-associate); 2 years (preference with associate).

7.14.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: ONSET OF INSOLVENCY: The look-back periods run from the 'onset of insolvency' — not from the date of the winding-up order. Onset = date of presentation of petition for winding up, or date of passing of resolution for voluntary winding up.

CONNECTED PERSONS (s.249 IA 1986): includes director; shadow director; associate (spouse/civil partner; relatives; partners; companies controlled by director). The presumption of intent/desire to prefer ONLY applies to connected persons — it is rebuttable.

TRANSACTION AT UNDERVALUE — DEFENCE: No order if the company entered the transaction in good faith for business purposes AND at the time there were reasonable grounds to believe it would benefit the company.

AVOIDANCE OF FLOATING CHARGE (s.245): The charge is NOT void if the company received new consideration (new money, goods or services) at or after creation of the charge. The charge is only valid to the extent of the new money. Interest on pre-existing debt is NOT new consideration.

PRESCRIBED PART CALCULATION (s.176A): 50% of the first £10,000 of net floating charge property + 20% of any remainder, capped at £800,000 (for charges created after 6 April 2020). It is set aside BEFORE paying the floating charge holder the remainder. The floating charge holder cannot waive the prescribed part.

WRONGFUL TRADING (s 214 / s 246ZB) — moved from 7.13: two limbs, BOTH required. (1) At some time BEFORE the commencement of the winding up the directors KNEW OR OUGHT TO HAVE CONCLUDED there was no reasonable prospect of avoiding insolvent liquidation (or administration). (2) They did NOT take EVERY STEP with a view to minimising the potential loss to creditors — limb 2 is the DEFENCE a director can advance. Insolvency here is measured on the BALANCE SHEET test. RESIGNING does NOT prevent liability; a dissenting director should have their concerns recorded in the board minutes. The IP has a 6-YEAR limitation period. Relief for honest and reasonable conduct under CA 2006 s 1157 is NOT available for wrongful trading.

FRAUDULENT TRADING (s 213 / s 246ZA) — moved from 7.13: requires ACTUAL DISHONESTY — carrying on the business with intent to defraud creditors or for any fraudulent purpose (e.g. ordering goods knowing they cannot be paid for). Harder to prove than wrongful trading, which needs no dishonesty. ANY PERSON knowingly party to it can be liable, not just directors. Criminal proceedings are also possible: CA 2006 s 993. Both fraudulent and wrongful trading can lead to a DISQUALIFICATION ORDER under the Company Directors Disqualification Act 1986.

7.13.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: TWO SEPARATE INSOLVENCY TESTS (s 123): (1) CASH FLOW — unable to pay debts as they fall due (s 123(1)(e)). (2) BALANCE SHEET — liabilities, INCLUDING contingent and prospective liabilities, exceed assets (s 123(2)). EITHER alone is sufficient. A company can fail one and pass the other. Creditors normally rely on the cash flow test because they cannot see the balance sheet.

STATUTORY DEMAND — MORE THAN £750, 3 WEEKS: the demand must be for MORE than £750 (not '£750 or more'), served on the company's REGISTERED OFFICE, and unpaid with no repayment arrangement after 3 WEEKS. An unsatisfied judgment where execution has been attempted is the alternative evidence (s 123(1)(b)).

ADMINISTRATION IMPOSES A MORATORIUM; LIQUIDATION DOES NOT: administration is a RESCUE process whose primary objective is to rescue the company as a going concern, and its main advantage is the statutory moratorium stopping enforcement of security and legal proceedings. Liquidation ends the company's existence and carries NO automatic moratorium.

ADMINISTRATION HIERARCHY IS STRICT (Sch B1 para 3): on appointment the administrator must consider ONLY objective 1 (rescue as a going concern). Objective 2 (better result for creditors as a whole than winding up) is reached only if objective 1 is not reasonably practicable OR objective 2 would give creditors a better outcome. Objective 3 (realise assets for secured/preferential creditors) only if NEITHER 1 nor 2 is reasonably practicable. If none can be achieved, administration cannot continue and immediate liquidation is the likely outcome.

CVA VOTING — WATCH THE OVERRIDE: 75% or more IN VALUE of UNSECURED creditors must agree (secured creditors are excluded from the vote). BUT the proposal fails if those voting against include MORE THAN 50% in value of all the UNCONNECTED creditors who vote. Do not stop at '75%'.

CVA — NO COURT APPROVAL AND NO MORATORIUM: the nominee MAY need to report to the court on viability, but there is NO requirement for court approval. A CVA generally does NOT give a statutory moratorium — that is administration's advantage. Directors REMAIN in office; the nominee becomes the SUPERVISOR.

WHO IS BOUND BY A CVA: all creditors, including those who did not vote — EXCEPT secured or preferential creditors who disagreed. Contrast a RESTRUCTURING PLAN, which on court SANCTION binds ALL creditors INCLUDING secured ones. That is the plan's advantage over a CVA.

MVL v CVL — THE DECLARATION IS THE DIVIDING LINE: an MVL is available ONLY to a SOLVENT company and requires the majority of directors to make a statutory declaration of solvency (s 89) that all debts will be paid in full WITH INTEREST within 12 months; the SHAREHOLDERS then control the process and choose the liquidator. In a CVL the company is INSOLVENT and the CREDITORS take over the process INCLUDING the choice of liquidator. If an MVL is begun and insolvency emerges, it MUST convert to a CVL.
WHO CAN PETITION FOR COMPULSORY LIQUIDATION: a creditor owed more than £750 (the usual petitioner), the COMPANY ITSELF, the company's DIRECTORS, an ADMINISTRATOR, or an OFFICIAL RECEIVER.

MORATORIUM IS NOT A PAYMENT HOLIDAY FOR EVERYONE: under the CIGA 2020 moratorium, all creditors EXCEPT FINANCIAL creditors are barred from enforcement. Sums due to FINANCIAL creditors (bank loans, mortgages) must STILL be paid as they fall due. Directors remain in control; the MONITOR (an IP) supervises and can end it by filing notice at court.

MORATORIUM ENTITIES: available to COMPANIES and LLPs, not to general or limited partnerships. Barred if there has been a moratorium, CVA or administration in the last 12 months, or the entity is already in an insolvency process.

FIXED-ASSET RECEIVER OWES DUTIES TO THE APPOINTING CREDITOR: the receiver's primary duty is to the creditor who appointed them, so they prioritise that client's interests over the company's or other creditors'. Contrast the ADMINISTRATOR, who acts on behalf of ALL creditors and NOT as agent for the charge holder — even when appointed by a qualifying floating charge holder.

OUT-OF-COURT ADMINISTRATION IS BLOCKED BY A PENDING PETITION: if a winding-up petition is outstanding (or an administration application is outstanding, or an administrative receiver is appointed, or the company is in liquidation), the company and its directors cannot use the out-of-court route.

CLAW-BACK AND THE FULL WATERFALL ARE IN 7.14: transactions at an undervalue (s 238), preferences (s 239), avoidance of floating charges (s 245), extortionate credit (s 244), fraudulent trading (s 213), wrongful trading (s 214) and misfeasance (s 212) all belong to chapter 7.14, together with the detailed order of distribution.

7.12.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: PROFIT vs REVENUE: Revenue (turnover) is total sales income. Gross profit = Revenue − Cost of Sales. Operating profit = Gross profit − operating expenses. Net profit (PAT) = profit after interest and tax. Don't confuse these levels.
BALANCE SHEET EQUATION: Assets = Liabilities + Equity (shareholders' funds). Net assets = Total assets − Total liabilities. Net assets must equal shareholders' funds (capital + reserves).

DEPRECIATION: Not a cash cost — reduces asset book value and profits annually. The actual cash was spent when the asset was purchased (capital expenditure). Depreciation affects the balance sheet (reduces asset value) and the P&L (reduces profit).

FILING DEADLINES: Private company — 9 months after accounting reference date. Public company — 6 months. Failure: automatic civil penalties on the company. Directors can face fines. The accounting reference date can be changed but the new deadline is calculated from the new date.

CURRENT RATIO vs ACID TEST: Current ratio = Current assets / Current liabilities (includes stock/inventory). Acid test (quick ratio) = (Current assets − Stock) / Current liabilities. Acid test is more conservative — excludes stock as it may be hard to convert to cash quickly.

DEBTOR DAYS: (Trade receivables / Revenue) × 365. Lower = better (collecting cash quickly). CREDITOR DAYS: (Trade payables / Cost of sales) × 365. Higher = better (paying suppliers later, conserving cash). ROCE: Return on Capital Employed = Operating profit / Capital employed × 100 — measures efficiency of capital use.

7.11.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: DISTRIBUTABLE PROFITS (s.830): The test is ACCUMULATED realised profits LESS accumulated realised losses — not just current year profits. A company can have made a profit this year but still have no distributable profits if prior losses exceed it. Capital profits are NOT distributable.

PUBLIC COMPANIES — ADDITIONAL TEST (s.831): Public companies have an extra restriction — net assets must not fall below the sum of the called-up share capital and undistributable reserves. This is stricter than for private companies.

INTERIM vs FINAL DIVIDEND: Final dividend — directors recommend, shareholders approve by ordinary resolution (before paying). Interim dividend — directors alone can declare and pay without shareholder approval. Both require distributable profits.

UNLAWFUL DIVIDEND: If paid out of capital (no distributable profits), the dividend is unlawful. RECOVERABLE from any shareholder who knew (or had reasonable grounds to believe) it was unlawful. Shareholders who received in good faith with no reasonable grounds to suspect unlawfulness cannot be forced to repay.

SHARE BUYBACK OUT OF CAPITAL (private companies only): Requires (a) directors' solvency statement AND (b) special resolution of shareholders. Creditors have 5 weeks to apply to court to object. Public companies cannot use this route — must use distributable profits or proceeds of new issue.
CAPITAL REDUCTION (s.641): Private companies can use the solvency statement route (no court order needed). Public companies must use the court-confirmed route (creditors can object).

7.10.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: REGISTRATION IS VOLUNTARY, BUT: the Companies Act 2006 provides a VOLUNTARY system of registration — nothing compels a charge holder to register. The trap is the consequence: an unregistered or incorrectly registered charge is VOID against the liquidator, administrator and other creditors, and the holder drops to UNSECURED. Do not say registration is mandatory; say failure to register destroys the security.

21 DAYS RUNS FROM THE DAY AFTER: Form MR01, the certified copy of the instrument and the fee must reach Companies House within 21 days of the day AFTER the day the charge was CREATED (s 859A(4)) — not the day of creation, and not the date of the loan drawdown.

FIXED BEATS FLOATING REGARDLESS OF DATE: a fixed charge takes priority over a floating charge over the same asset EVEN IF the floating charge was created first. This is the single most tested priority point. The only answer that reverses it is a NEGATIVE PLEDGE of which the later lender had actual notice.

CREATION, NOT REGISTRATION, DECIDES PRIORITY BETWEEN EQUALS: as between two registered fixed charges (or two registered floating charges) over the same asset, priority is by date of CREATION. Registration decides whether you are secured at all; creation decides who ranks first.

CRYSTALLISATION DOES NOT PROMOTE A FLOATING CHARGE: on crystallisation the floating charge attaches to the assets in the class and is enforceable AS a fixed charge — but it is NOT classed as a fixed charge for the ORDER OF PRIORITY OF PAYMENTS. It still ranks as a floating charge in the insolvency waterfall.

MORTGAGE v CHARGE: a mortgage TRANSFERS TITLE in the asset to the lender (returning on repayment) and is the most secure form. A charge grants only an EQUITABLE right over the charged property — the lender gets NO proprietary interest, only the right to stop the borrower dealing with the asset and to be paid ahead of unsecured creditors.

LIEN HAS NO POWER OF SALE: a lien is the creditor's right to keep PHYSICAL POSSESSION of the debtor's goods until the debt is repaid. It does NOT entitle the creditor to sell the goods and apply the proceeds. If an option says the lien holder may sell, it is wrong.
ONLY A COMPANY OR LLP CAN GRANT A FLOATING CHARGE: because only they are separate legal entities capable of owning the assets. A sole trader or a general partnership cannot.

LAND MUST BE REGISTERED TWICE: a mortgage or fixed charge over registered land goes on the Land Registry AND the Companies House register. If it is NOT registered at the Land Registry, a buyer takes the land FREE of the charge — even if the buyer knew of the charge and even if it appeared on the Companies House register.
A DEBENTURE IS A DOCUMENT, NOT A DEBT: in this context 'debenture' means the security/charging instrument creating fixed and/or floating charges — not the loan or a type of bond.

OVERDRAFTS ARE THE EXPENSIVE OPTION: overdrafts cost MORE than term loans precisely because they are usually UNSECURED and therefore riskier for the bank. Interest is compound and unpaid interest is added to capital. Repayable on demand, no notice required.

DIRECTORS HAVE THE BORROWING POWER: under the Model Articles the directors manage the company and so have the general power to borrow and grant security. The Model Articles impose NO restriction on borrowing — but the articles CAN be amended to insert one, and existing loan agreements may restrict further borrowing.

7.9B.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: CHARGE REGISTRATION (s.859A): registration is VOLUNTARY, BUT a charge not registered within 21 days (Form MR01 + certified copy of the instrument + fee) is VOID against a liquidator/administrator and other creditors — the debt itself survives but the lender ranks as UNSECURED. A later lender who DOES register takes priority over an earlier unregistered charge.

FIXED vs FLOATING PRIORITY: a fixed charge ALWAYS ranks ahead of a floating charge over the same asset — even if the floating charge was created FIRST — UNLESS a negative pledge in the floating charge documentation (of which the later lender has notice) subordinates the later fixed charge. Two fixed (or two floating) charges rank by DATE OF CREATION, not date of registration.

CRYSTALLISATION: a floating charge crystallises on a specified event (default or insolvency), then attaches to the assets and is enforceable like a fixed charge — but it is NOT treated as a fixed charge for the ORDER OF PRIORITY of payments.

DEBENTURE: it is simply the NAME of the security/charging document (instrument) — NOT a type of charge. It typically creates fixed and/or floating charges plus covenants, a negative pledge and events of default.

NEGATIVE PLEDGE: borrower's promise not to grant later security ranking above the floating charge. Binds a later lender only if that lender has NOTICE — achieved by noting it on Form MR01 and in the charge document (public at Companies House). A later chargee with notice ranks behind and may be liable in tort for inducing breach of contract.

MORTGAGE OVER LAND: must be by DEED (LPA 1925 s.87) and registered TWICE (Land Registry + Companies House). If NOT registered at the Land Registry, a buyer takes the land FREE of the charge — even with knowledge and even if it appears on the Companies House register.

LIEN vs the rest: a lien is ONLY a right to retain possession until paid — it does NOT allow the creditor to sell the goods. A guarantee is not strictly a form of security but is treated with securities.

7.9.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: OLD vs NEW COMPANY (the key trap): "Incorporated BEFORE 1 October 2009" = OLD company → may still carry an Authorised Share Capital (ASC) cap moved from its memorandum into its articles by s.28 (remove by ORDINARY resolution), and it does NOT get automatic s.550 authority — a private one-class OLD company must FIRST pass an ordinary resolution to grant s.550 authority (permanent thereafter). "On/after 1 October 2009" = NEW company → no ASC, no cap unless the articles say so, and a private one-class company has AUTOMATIC s.550 authority.

ALLOTMENT AUTHORITY — s.550 vs s.551: automatic s.550 authority is ONLY for a private company with ONE class of shares (and, if old, only after the enabling ordinary resolution). Multiple classes, public companies → always need s.551 authority: ordinary resolution stating max shares + expiry (max 5 years, renewable), filed at Companies House.

ALLOTTED vs ISSUED: shares are ALLOTTED when a person gains the unconditional right to be entered in the register of members (s.558); ISSUED when that allotment is actually registered. The exam may test the distinction — don't treat them as identical.

PRE-EMPTION RIGHTS — s.561: triggered ONLY by a NEW CASH issue of equity securities (ordinary shares). Does NOT apply to: non-cash consideration (s.565); bonus shares; employee share scheme shares. Existing shareholders offered pro rata for 14 days before shares go elsewhere.

DISAPPLICATION of pre-emption: by SPECIAL resolution (ss.570–571), or permanently in the articles / by SR for a private company with one class (s.569). A special-resolution disapplication lasts only as long as the allotment authority it is linked to.

SHARES AT A DISCOUNT (s.580): strictly PROHIBITED. Allotment below nominal value is void; purchaser liable to pay the discount + interest; director/company commit a criminal offence. Public companies must obtain an INDEPENDENT valuation of non-cash consideration; private companies need not (the loophole).

7.8.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: BOARD WRITTEN RESOLUTION requires UNANIMITY — all eligible directors must sign. Written resolutions in a shareholders' context require only the relevant majority (50% or 75%). Don't confuse the two.

14 CLEAR DAYS' NOTICE for a general meeting: 'clear days' excludes the day notice is given AND the day of the meeting. If notice is sent on Monday, the first clear day is Tuesday; 14 clear days means the meeting can be held at the earliest on the 16th day.
SHORT NOTICE: Valid if agreed by (a) majority in NUMBER of shareholders AND (b) that majority holds ≥90% of voting shares. It is not simply majority by shares alone.

WRITTEN RESOLUTIONS — LAPSE DATE: The resolution lapses 28 days from the circulation date unless a different period is specified. Votes received after the lapse date are not counted. Resolution passes as soon as the required threshold is reached — not at the end of the period.

QUORUM AT GENERAL MEETING: 2 shareholders (unless single-member company: quorum = 1). If inquorate, meeting cannot proceed. Quorum at BOARD meeting: 2 directors (Model Article 11), BUT an interested director may be excluded from quorum and voting.
CHAIRPERSON CASTING VOTE: At board meetings, chairperson has casting vote on a deadlock (Model Article 13). At general meetings, the chairperson generally has NO casting vote.

7.7.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: s 175 vs s 177 — THE CORE DISTINCTION. s 175 = SITUATIONAL conflicts (company property, information, a corporate opportunity). s 177 = a conflict arising from a PROPOSED TRANSACTION WITH THE COMPANY ITSELF, which s 175 expressly does NOT cover. Getting the section wrong is the commonest error in this chapter.

s 175 CAN BE AUTHORISED BY THE BOARD; s 176 CANNOT. For s 175, in a private company the board may authorise if the QUORUM is met and the interested director is NOT COUNTED. For s 176 there is no power to authorise at all — only the SHAREHOLDERS can RATIFY, and only AFTER the benefit has been received.

s 177 vs s 182 — CIVIL vs CRIMINAL. s 177 (proposed) failure makes the contract VOIDABLE and the director accountable for profits. s 182 (existing) failure is a CRIMINAL OFFENCE — a fine on indictment, or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum summarily.

s 172 IS SUBJECTIVE: 'in the way HE CONSIDERS, in good faith'. The six listed factors are NON-EXHAUSTIVE and NO SINGLE FACTOR carries more weight than any other. Directors must give due consideration to every relevant factor — not a box-ticking exercise — and MINUTE the discussion for evidential purposes.

s 174 — THE HIGHER STANDARD WINS. The objective test (a reasonably diligent person carrying out the same functions in relation to that company) sets the MINIMUM. The subjective test raises it where the director actually has more: a finance director who is a qualified accountant is held to the standard of a reasonably diligent qualified accountant.
A LOAN IS NOT A NON-CASH ASSET. So a loan to a director is never an SPT — it is dealt with under s 197, not s 190. Cash includes FOREIGN CURRENCY.

SPT THRESHOLD — READ IT CAREFULLY: value exceeds £100,000, OR exceeds 10% of net assets AND is more than £5,000. The £5,000 floor attaches ONLY to the percentage limb. No statutory accounts: use CALLED-UP SHARE CAPITAL instead of net assets.
SPT APPROVAL CAN COME AFTERWARDS — but only if the transaction was made CONDITIONAL on obtaining shareholder approval. Otherwise approval must precede entry.

NO APPROVAL DOES NOT MEAN VOID — it means VOIDABLE at the COMPANY'S choosing, and it can be AFFIRMED within a reasonable time by ordinary resolution. Three bars stop avoidance — see the decision tree above.
ACCOUNT AND INDEMNIFY APPLY EITHER WAY — whether or not the transaction is avoided. But a connected person or authorising director who DID NOT KNOW of the contravention is NOT LIABLE.
RATIFICATION — THE VOTES ARE STRIPPED OUT: general meeting, disregarded (s 239(4)); written resolution, not eligible members at all (s 239(3)).

s 1157 RELIEF IS DISCRETIONARY AND CUMULATIVE — the court MAY relieve only if the director acted HONESTLY, AND REASONABLY, AND ought fairly to be excused having regard to all the circumstances. All three, not any one.
SOLE DIRECTOR: no s 177 declaration is required (there are no other directors to declare to), provided the articles permit a sole director.

MODEL ARTICLE 14: an interested director does not count towards the QUORUM and cannot VOTE on the matter — unless disapplied one-off by ORDINARY resolution, permitted by the articles, or removed permanently by SPECIAL resolution.

DUTIES ARE OWED TO THE COMPANY, NOT TO INDIVIDUAL SHAREHOLDERS. Only the company enforces; a shareholder's route is a DERIVATIVE CLAIM on the company's behalf. (For directors' exposure to creditors on insolvency — wrongful trading and the duty to put creditors first — see 7.14, not this chapter.)

7.6.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: s 168 CANNOT BE EXCLUDED: shareholders can ALWAYS remove a director by ordinary resolution, whatever the service contract or the articles say. The articles may ADD further methods of removal, but cannot take this one away.

BUT REMOVAL IS NOT FREE: it does NOT deprive the director of compensation for loss of office, damages for termination of the directorship, or any rights as an EMPLOYEE. Removing and paying are separate questions.
NO WRITTEN RESOLUTION - s 288(2)(a). The director has a right to respond, so it must be a general meeting. This is a favourite distractor.

SPECIAL NOTICE IS 28 CLEAR DAYS, given BY the shareholder TO the company at its registered office - it is not notice of the meeting. Watch the s 312(4) twist: shareholders are DEEMED to have given proper special notice even if the directors choose to hold the GM SOONER than 28 clear days.
THE BOARD CANNOT REMOVE A DIRECTOR UNDER THE MODEL ARTICLES. Board dismissal by majority vote exists only if the articles expressly provide for it.

s 303 REQUISITION = 5% of paid-up share capital. Then 21 DAYS for the directors to CALL the meeting, and the meeting held within 28 DAYS OF THE DECISION TO CALL - not 28 days of the notice. If they still refuse, shareholders call it themselves, held within 3 MONTHS of the ORIGINAL request.
EXPENSES: shareholders who had to call the meeting recover from the COMPANY, which then recovers from the DIRECTORS PERSONALLY.

BUSHELL v FAITH: weighted votes on a resolution for their OWN removal. Only bites if the director is ALSO a shareholder - directors cannot vote at a GM in their capacity as director. It does NOT apply in a company on unamended Model Articles. Correctly drafted, it makes the director irremovable - check for a SECOND weighted clause protecting the special resolution to amend the articles.

SERVICE CONTRACT OVER 2 YEARS - s 188: shareholder approval required. Under Model Articles this is an ORDINARY resolution. Note the board, not the shareholders, sets remuneration under the Model Articles.
TM01 WITHIN 14 DAYS to the Registrar once the person ceases to be a director.

s 6 CDDA UNFITNESS has TWO limbs and both are needed: (a) was or is a director of a company that BECAME INSOLVENT, and (b) conduct makes them unfit. The manual frames the court's power to disqualify as DISCRETIONARY, and the factors go to whether to make an order AND for how long.
DISQUALIFICATION RANGE IS 2-15 YEARS. Contravening an order is a CRIMINAL offence AND makes the person personally liable for all the relevant debts of the company they are managing.

PERMISSION TO ACT WHILE DISQUALIFIED comes with two conditions: someone professionally qualified on the board (e.g. an accountant) must keep an eye on them, AND they must accept PERSONAL LIABILITY for the company's debts.
ECCTA 2023: appointing a disqualified person as a director is VOID unless there is court permission or a government licence.

7.5.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps - Common Errors
body: DERIVATIVE CLAIM - THE REMEDY GOES TO THE COMPANY, NOT THE SHAREHOLDER. This is the single most-tested distinction against s 994, where the petitioner personally gets the buy-out. If the stem asks what the claimant recovers, check who was wronged.

PERMISSION IS AUTOMATICALLY REFUSED in three situations: a s 172-compliant director would not continue the claim; the act was pre-authorised; the company has ratified it. Everything else is discretionary - do not treat the good-faith factor as a bar.
STAGE 1 IS A PAPER EXERCISE: the court MUST dismiss if the evidence discloses no prima facie case. There is no hearing at that stage.

UNFAIR PREJUDICE NEEDS BOTH LIMBS - unfair AND prejudicial, on a NON-TRIVIAL breach. Mere disagreement with a commercial decision is not enough, and the petitioner must be acting IN THEIR CAPACITY AS A SHAREHOLDER (not as a director or employee).
s 994 COVERS ANTICIPATED FUTURE CONDUCT as well as past and present - a proposed act or omission is enough.
TWO SITUATIONS WHERE UNFAIR PREJUDICE IS DISALLOWED: a binding arbitration agreement, and a shareholder who voluntarily severed links then petitions to get the best price for their shares.

JUST AND EQUITABLE WINDING UP IS A LAST RESORT - s 125 IA 1986. If a s 994 buy-out would do, the court will refuse. The petitioner must also show a TANGIBLE BENEFIT. Do not pick winding up simply because the facts show deadlock.
SHOW OF HANDS vs POLL: one vote per SHAREHOLDER on a show of hands, one vote per SHARE on a poll. A majority holder outvoted on a show of hands demands a POLL to win - a classic stem.
THE 10% POLL RIGHT CANNOT BE EXCLUDED by the articles (s 321(1)) except for electing the chair or adjourning. Do not accept an article that purports to remove it generally.

MIND THE THRESHOLDS: 5% to circulate a resolution or call a meeting, 10% to demand a poll, more than 25% to BLOCK a special resolution, more than 50% for majority rule, 75% to pass a special resolution. The 25% blocking stake is the one most often missed.
YOU ARE ONLY A SHAREHOLDER ONCE ENTERED ON THE REGISTER OF MEMBERS. A share certificate is merely PRIMA FACIE evidence - it does not confer membership.

s 33 BINDS SHAREHOLDERS TO EACH OTHER as well as to the company, but PRIVITY blocks third parties - a person suing in a capacity other than member (e.g. as solicitor to the company) cannot enforce the articles.

A SHAREHOLDERS' AGREEMENT CANNOT DICTATE HOW SHAREHOLDER-DIRECTORS VOTE AS DIRECTORS, and must not fetter the company's powers. Its advantage over the articles is that it is NOT filed and stays confidential.
THE IRREGULARITY PRINCIPLE: if the majority could simply ratify the irregularity, no claim lies. Check for ratifiability before reaching for any remedy.

7.4.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: PRE-INCORPORATION CONTRACTS: A company cannot be bound by a contract made before it was incorporated (Kelner v Baxter). The promoter is personally liable on the contract unless there is a novation after incorporation or the third party releases the promoter.

CERTIFICATE OF INCORPORATION: Conclusive evidence that the company is duly registered (s.15 CA 2006). Any defect in the registration process is cured. The company exists from the date stated on the certificate.

ARTICLES OF ASSOCIATION: The default model articles (prescribed by SI 2008/3229) apply unless excluded/altered. The articles constitute a contract between the company and its members and between members inter se — BUT only in their capacity as members (Hickman v Kent).
SINGLE-MEMBER PRIVATE COMPANY: Lawful since 1992. Decisions of the sole member must be recorded in writing unless made at a general meeting. Minutes or written resolution should be kept.

TRADING CERTIFICATE: A public company (plc) CANNOT trade or borrow until it has received a trading certificate under s.761 CA 2006 confirming its allotted share capital is not less than the authorised minimum (£50,000 for a plc). This does NOT apply to private companies.

COMPANY NAME: Must end in 'Limited' or 'Ltd' (private) or 'Public Limited Company' or 'plc' (public). Certain 'sensitive' words require prior approval. Name must not be the same as or too like an existing registered name.

COMPANY NAME CHANGE — SPECIAL RESOLUTION (MODEL ARTICLES): Under the Model Articles (default), changing a company's registered name requires a SPECIAL resolution (75% of votes cast). An ordinary resolution (simple majority) is NOT sufficient. Always check whether Model Articles apply. See 7.4.4.3 and 7.4.6.

7.3.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors

items: Place a notice in the London Gazette → protects against NEW creditors who had no prior dealings with the firm

Give ACTUAL NOTICE to EXISTING creditors/suppliers who dealt with the firm while the partner was a member. An indemnity from co-partners protects the retired partner internally but does NOT extinguish third-party liability. Removing your name from stationery alone is NOT sufficient
body.head: RETIRING PARTNER — EXISTING vs NEW CREDITORS: On retirement, a partner remains liable for debts incurred BEFORE retirement. To limit future liability

body: PARTNER EXPULSION — NO WRITTEN AGREEMENT: Under the Partnership Act 1890, there is NO default power to expel a partner. Expulsion is only possible if the partnership agreement expressly provides for it (PA 1890 s.25). Where there is no written agreement (partnership at will), a partner CANNOT be expelled against their will — dissolution is the only remedy. Even where an agreement exists, expulsion requires a MAJORITY (not merely plurality) unless the agreement specifies otherwise. If all partners must agree under the agreement, unanimity is required.

LAW GRADUATE — RIGHT OF AUDIENCE IN MAGISTRATES: Rights of audience are a reserved legal activity under the LSA 2007. A law graduate who is not admitted or authorised cannot exercise rights of audience as of right. ⚠ DELEGATION UPDATE — Mazur v Charles Russell Speechlys LLP [2026] EWCA Civ 369: litigation tasks may be carried out by non-authorised persons PROVIDED they act under genuine supervision and overall responsibility of an authorised person (e.g. solicitor). Independent conduct of litigation by an unauthorised person is a criminal offence under LSA 2007. HOWEVER, the magistrates' court has a discretionary power to GRANT permission to an unqualified person to represent a defendant in specific circumstances. The correct answer is 'yes, if the court grants permission' — not that it is automatically permissible or automatically forbidden.

7.2.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors

items: Profits and losses shared equally regardless of capital contribution
All partners have equal management rights
No partner is entitled to a salary
A new partner cannot be admitted without unanimous consent
body.head: PARTNERSHIP ACT 1890 — DEFAULT RULES: PA 1890 applies in the absence of a contrary agreement. Key defaults

body: ACTUAL vs APPARENT AUTHORITY: An act done in the ordinary course of a firm's business binds the firm (s.8 PA 1890) unless the partner had no authority AND the third party knew this.
