Holding out (s.14): if a person holds out another as a partner, they are bound to third parties who relied on that representation.

PARTNERSHIP PROPERTY: Property brought into the firm or acquired FOR the purposes of the firm AND in furtherance of the firm's business = partnership property (s.20). Partners hold it on trust for the firm. Distinct from property used by the firm but retained personally by a partner.

DISSOLUTION vs RETIREMENT: Dissolution terminates the partnership (PA 1890 s.32-44). In a partnership at will, any partner can dissolve by notice. A partnership agreement may restrict dissolution to specific events. A retiring partner remains liable for debts incurred before retirement unless released by novation.

LIMITED LIABILITY PARTNERSHIPS (LLPs): Created by LLP Act 2000. Members have limited liability; treated as a body corporate. Governed by the members' agreement (default rules in Limited Liability Partnerships Regulations 2001). Designated members have additional filing duties.

GOODWILL ON DISSOLUTION: Unless the partnership agreement provides otherwise, the goodwill is an asset of the firm to be realised and distributed. A non-competition clause in a dissolution agreement is subject to restraint of trade principles.

PARTNERSHIP EXPULSION — NO AGREEMENT = NO EXPULSION: Without a written partnership agreement providing for expulsion, a partner CANNOT be expelled. Where an agreement does allow expulsion, it typically requires a UNANIMOUS vote of ALL partners (not majority, not 'the other partners'). Death, bankruptcy, or notice may dissolve the partnership — they do not 'expel'. See 7.2.7.1, 7.2.9 and 7.2.10.

7.1.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: LLP NEEDS TWO MEMBERS; A COMPANY NEEDS ONE: an LLP is formed by AT LEAST TWO members, at least two of whom must be DESIGNATED members. A company can be formed by ONE or more persons. A stem offering 'one or more members' for an LLP is wrong.

PRE-INCORPORATION CONTRACTS — 'MAY REMAIN LIABLE', NOT 'WILL AUTOMATICALLY TRANSFER': the promoter is normally personally liable and is NOT automatically released on incorporation. Release requires NOVATION, which needs the consent of all parties INCLUDING the newly formed company. Never pick an option saying liability transfers automatically. See 7.1.3.

LIMITED PARTNER LOSES THE CAP IF THEY MANAGE: a limited partner's liability is capped at the capital contributed ONLY if they do not participate in the management of the LP's business. An LP must have AT LEAST ONE partner in EACH category.
UNLIMITED COMPANY MUST BE PRIVATE, AS MUST A COMPANY LIMITED BY GUARANTEE. Only a company limited by shares can be public. And only a PUBLIC company may offer its shares to the public.

PARTNERS CANNOT CONTRACT OUT OF CREDITOR LIABILITY: a partnership agreement can supplement or displace most Partnership Act 1890 provisions, but NOT the elements relating to partners' liability to creditors, which remains unlimited.

PARTNERSHIP ASSETS ARE NOT OWNED BY THE FIRM: a general partnership has no separate legal personality, so partners hold partnership assets in their OWN names as agents and trustees for the partnership. An LLP and a company own their own assets.
PUBLIC COMPANY OFFICER MINIMUMS: private company = at least ONE director. Public company = minimum TWO directors PLUS a company secretary.
A PERSONAL GUARANTEE IS NOT VEIL-PIERCING: a director who guaranteed the company's borrowing is liable under the GUARANTEE. Separate legal personality is untouched.

8.17.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: APPEAL DESTINATION: a COUNTY COURT DISTRICT JUDGE's decision is appealed to a CIRCUIT JUDGE (in the county court) — NOT to the High Court. A circuit judge's decision goes to a High Court judge; a High Court judge's to the Court of Appeal.

body.head: PERMISSION (first appeal, r.52.6) — granted if EITHER:
items: the appeal has a real prospect of success, OR
there is some other compelling reason (e.g. an important point of law to clarify)

body: SECOND APPEAL is much harder (r.52.7): permission from the COURT OF APPEAL only, and only if the appeal has a real prospect of success AND raises an important point of principle or practice, OR there is some other compelling reason. A first appeal is normally the final word.

GROUNDS (r.52.21(3)): an appeal is allowed only where the decision was (a) WRONG (error of fact or law), or (b) UNJUST due to a SERIOUS procedural irregularity — NOT because the appeal court would have exercised discretion differently. An appeal is a REVIEW, not a rehearing.
NO AUTOMATIC STAY: an appeal does not stay the order appealed (r.52.16) — the appellant must request a stay (granted mainly where enforcement would make the appeal pointless).
TAKING CONTROL OF GOODS — the court depends on the debt: >£5,000 → High Court writ of control; £600–£5,000 → High Court OR county court; <£600 → county court warrant of control.
INSOLVENCY THRESHOLDS: a company can be wound up on a debt over £750; an individual can be made bankrupt on a debt of £5,000 or more. Judgment creditors are UNSECURED, so recovery may be a fraction.

8.16.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: CLAIMANT BEATS OWN Pt 36 OFFER (r.36.17(4)): from expiry of the relevant period the defendant pays — (1) costs on the INDEMNITY basis; (2) up to 10% interest above base on those costs; (3) up to 10% interest above base on the SUM AWARDED; and (4) an ADDITIONAL AMOUNT up to £75,000 (10% of award up to £500k, then 5% of the excess). 'Unjust' is a HIGH bar.

CLAIMANT FAILS TO BEAT DEFENDANT'S Pt 36 OFFER (r.36.17(3)): defendant pays claimant's costs UP TO the end of the relevant period; then the CLAIMANT pays the defendant's costs (standard basis) PLUS interest from expiry onward — even though the claimant WON. The claimant does not have to pay indemnity costs (no enhanced uplift against a claimant).

DISCONTINUANCE permission is NOT triggered merely by a defence being filed. Permission/consent is needed only where: an interim injunction was granted; an undertaking was given; the claimant received an interim payment; or there is more than one claimant. Default costs rule: the claimant pays the defendant's costs.
DEFENDANT'S Pt 36 MONEY OFFER = a SINGLE SUM payable within 14 DAYS of acceptance (r.36.6). It cannot be by instalments or over a longer period — a reason to use a Calderbank offer instead.

Pt 36 IS A SELF-CONTAINED CODE — ordinary contract rules don't apply. A counter-offer does NOT reject/kill a Pt 36 offer; it can still be accepted (if not withdrawn) even after later offers. It stays open until trial unless formally withdrawn or time-limited.
Pt 36 costs consequences DON'T apply if the offer was made <21 days before trial, was withdrawn, was amended to be less advantageous, or was accepted.
MEDIATION / plain 'without prejudice' offers are NOT admissible on costs — only 'WP save as to costs' (Calderbank) or Pt 36 offers are.

8.15.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: FIXED RECOVERABLE COSTS (from 1 Oct 2023) apply to the FAST and INTERMEDIATE tracks — NOT the multi-track. Fast track FRC: damages ≤ £25,000 and trial ≤ 1 day. Amount depends on the complexity BAND (1–4) and the stage reached. Small claims generally recover NO legal costs (only disbursements / unreasonable-conduct costs).

STANDARD vs INDEMNITY — the proportionality test is the key difference. STANDARD: costs disallowed if unreasonably incurred, unreasonable in amount, OR disproportionate (even if reasonable); doubt resolved for the PAYING party (recover ≈70%). INDEMNITY: no proportionality filter; doubt resolved for the RECEIVING party (recover ≈80%). If the order is silent, it is the STANDARD basis.

CLAIMANT BEATS OWN Pt 36 OFFER (r.36.17(4)): from expiry of the relevant period — indemnity costs, up to 10% interest above base on those costs AND on the sum awarded, plus an additional amount up to £75,000 (10% up to £500k, 5% of the excess). Applies unless UNJUST (high bar).

CLAIMANT FAILS TO BEAT DEFENDANT'S Pt 36 OFFER (r.36.17(3)): claimant (though the winner) pays the defendant's costs from expiry of the relevant period plus interest; the defendant pays the claimant's costs only up to expiry.

INDEMNITY PRINCIPLE: a party recovers only costs it is actually liable to pay. Under a CFA/DBA, base costs are still recoverable from the opponent, BUT the success fee is NOT recoverable from the opponent.

SUMMARY vs DETAILED ASSESSMENT: summary = by the judge at the end of a hearing (norm for fast track trials and hearings ≤1 day). Detailed = line-by-line by a costs judge (norm for multi-track trials / hearings >1 day), which must COMMENCE within 3 months of judgment; the court usually orders an interim payment on account meanwhile.

NON-PARTY COSTS (SCA 1981 s.51): available against a funder who controls/benefits (e.g. an owner-director, professional funder, insurer) — but NOT 'pure funders' such as family or friends who don't stand to benefit.

8.14.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: LEADING vs NON-LEADING: cross-examination uses LEADING questions (by the OPPONENT); examination-in-chief and RE-examination use NON-leading questions (by the witness's OWN side). Re-examination is confined to matters ARISING in cross-examination — no new topics.
TRIAL BUNDLE MUST NOT CONTAIN Pt 36 or 'without prejudice save as to costs' OFFERS. The court must not see them until after judgment (on costs). Including them is a serious error.

WITNESS SUMMONS TIMING: the court's permission is needed if the summons is issued LESS THAN 7 DAYS before trial, or for any hearing OTHER than the trial (r.34.3(2)). Conduct money (travel/lost earnings) must be offered when served (r.34.7); a recipient can apply to set it aside on ≥2 days' notice.
MODES OF ADDRESS: High Court judge = 'My Lord'/'My Lady'; district judge (county court) = 'Judge'. Witnesses address ANSWERS to the JUDGE, not the questioner.

'PURDAH': once a witness starts giving evidence they must NOT discuss the case with anyone (including family, and their own solicitor) until released — even over adjournments/weekends. If the witness is also the client, the solicitor needs the court's express permission to take instructions.
WITNESS STATEMENT = EVIDENCE-IN-CHIEF (r.32.5): the witness confirms it rather than re-reading it; amplification or new matters need the court's permission (r.32.5(3)).

RES JUDICATA & HENDERSON v HENDERSON: a handed-down judgment bars re-litigating the same issues (absent appeal), and a party generally cannot later raise issues that SHOULD have been brought in the original proceedings.

8.13.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: COPYING IN A SOLICITOR does NOT create privilege. It is the SUBSTANCE of the communication that matters — privilege applies only if the dominant purpose was giving/receiving confidential legal advice. Cc'ing a lawyer on a commercial email changes nothing.

A PRE-EXISTING DOCUMENT is not made privileged by sending it to a solicitor. E.g. a historic email chain forwarded to a lawyer to seek advice does NOT thereby become privileged. Privilege attaches to the communication seeking/giving advice, not the underlying document.

LEGAL ADVICE PRIVILEGE ≠ ANY ADVISER. It covers lawyers (incl. legal executives and FOREIGN lawyers) but NOT non-lawyers — so an ACCOUNTANT'S TAX ADVICE is NOT covered by legal advice privilege. In-house counsel is covered only when advising in a LEGAL (not commercial/business) capacity.

'CLIENT' IS CONSTRUED NARROWLY. Interview notes of employees giving information as employees (not as the client seeking advice) may not attract legal advice privilege — though LITIGATION privilege may apply if a dispute is in prospect.

DOMINANT PURPOSE = THE COMMISSIONING PARTY'S, not the author's. A dual-purpose document (e.g. an accident/safety report made both for litigation and to improve safety) is NOT privileged unless litigation was the DOMINANT purpose.

WITHOUT PREJUDICE IS A JOINT PRIVILEGE — one party cannot waive it alone. It needs a genuine attempt to settle an existing dispute (labelling alone doesn't create it). The FACT of WP communications may be disclosable; the CONTENT almost never is.
COLLATERAL WAIVER ('cherry-picking'): waiving privilege in one document can waive it across RELATED documents, to prevent a party showing only a partial, favourable picture.

8.12.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: AN EMAIL + ITS ATTACHMENTS = ONE document. If some attachments are confidential and IRRELEVANT they must still be disclosed but can be REDACTED — you don't drop them.

REDACTED e-documents must NOT be produced in native or OCR form. A partially redacted document must be converted to a NEW IMAGE (e.g. PDF) with the redaction embedded — otherwise the opponent can 'look behind' the redaction in the metadata/native file.

KEYWORDS CANNOT BE CHOSEN UNILATERALLY. Search terms, custodians and date ranges should be AGREED with the other side; if agreement fails, seek the court's directions (PD 31B para 17). Terms need not be the same for both parties (e.g. don't search your OWN name — it captures everything).

CONTROL OF PERSONAL DEVICES/ACCOUNTS: an employer controls company-owned laptops/phones (right to inspect). A senior employee's PERSONAL device/email is NOT within the employer's control unless a contractual/fiduciary duty to deliver up the documents exists — otherwise a NON-PARTY disclosure order may be needed.

PRESERVATION arises as soon as litigation is contemplated — suspend document-retention/auto-deletion policies (PD 31B para 7) and stop routine shredding. Tampering/amending a relevant document breaches the duty and can be contempt.
NATIVE FORMAT is the default for producing electronic copies (with metadata) unless the parties agree otherwise.

TECHNOLOGY-ASSISTED REVIEW (predictive coding) is permissible on proportionality grounds but should be NOTIFIED and ideally AGREED in advance; if objected to, seek the court's approval (Pyrrho Investments v MWB Property).

8.11.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: TRACK DETERMINES THE REGIME (from 6 April 2024): FAST TRACK → standard disclosure under CPR r.31.6 (default). INTERMEDIATE & MULTI-TRACK → the menu/report procedure in CPR r.31.5(3)–(8) — UNLESS the claim includes personal injury, when standard disclosure applies. Don't assume 'standard disclosure' applies to every case.

PD 57AD MODEL A ≠ 'NO DISCLOSURE'. In the Business & Property Courts, Model A = disclosure of KNOWN ADVERSE documents only (no new searches). The models run A (known adverse) → B (limited: key docs + known adverse) → C (request-led) → D (narrow search-based, closest to standard disclosure) → E (wide, train-of-enquiry — exceptional only).

CONFIDENTIALITY IS NOT A GROUND TO WITHHOLD INSPECTION. If a document is relevant it must be produced; sensitivity is managed by redaction (confidentiality + IRRELEVANCE) or a 'confidentiality club/ring' — not by refusing inspection. Only privilege, loss of control, or disproportionality justify withholding (r.31.3).
DISCLOSE EXISTENCE vs ALLOW INSPECTION are two stages. A privileged document is still DISCLOSED (listed, by category, in N265 section 2 with the ground) — you withhold INSPECTION, not disclosure.

INADVERTENT INSPECTION (r.31.20): a privileged document produced by mistake cannot be used by the recipient without the court's permission, provided it was reasonably obvious it was sent in error. If NOT obvious, privilege may be treated as waived — so notify, don't read.

FALSE DISCLOSURE STATEMENT = CONTEMPT (r.31.23). Signing without an honest belief in its truth is contempt of court. A party who fails to disclose or wrongly withholds inspection may not rely on that document later without permission (r.31.21).

8.10.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: HEARSAY IS ADMISSIBLE IN CIVIL PROCEEDINGS (CEA 1995 s 1): failure to give a hearsay notice goes to WEIGHT, not admissibility. Contrast the criminal regime. The court attaches whatever weight it considers appropriate using the s 4 factors.

EXPERT EVIDENCE NEEDS PERMISSION (r 35.4) and the court DEFINES THE SCOPE. Anything outside that scope is INADMISSIBLE. The expert's OVERRIDING duty is to the COURT (r 35.3) — not to the party instructing or paying them, even a party-appointed expert.

AN EXPERT STRAYING OUTSIDE THEIR EXPERTISE DOES NOT LOSE THE WHOLE REPORT: where a report contains opinions outside the expert's area, the court TAKES ACCOUNT of that rather than excluding the whole report.

WITNESS SUMMARY IS NOT A WITNESS SUMMONS: a SUMMARY (r 32.9) is served where you cannot obtain a signed statement. A SUMMONS compels a witness to attend or produce documents. Different purpose, different rule.

SUMMARY JUDGMENT IS A HIGHER STANDARD: 'no real prospect of success' is higher than the balance of probabilities. 'Real' need not be substantial and CAN include an IMPROBABLE case, but must be more than merely arguable — a FANCIFUL case fails. Do not say the applicant must prove its case on the balance of probabilities.

CONTEMPT USES THE CRIMINAL STANDARD: the civil standard is the balance of probabilities, but contempt of court proceedings — INCLUDING CIVIL contempt — require proof beyond reasonable doubt, because a finding can lead to a custodial sentence.

AFFIDAVIT v WITNESS STATEMENT: an affidavit is SWORN and ends with a JURAT, not a statement of truth. Required for SEARCH ORDERS and FREEZING INJUNCTIONS (r 32.15). A false affidavit risks PERJURY (a criminal prosecution); a false statement of truth risks CONTEMPT (permission to bring proceedings required). Both carry an unlimited fine and up to 2 years' custody.

THE BURDEN CAN SHIFT ONTO THE DEFENDANT: the claimant proves the claim, but a defendant asserting a POSITIVE case bears the burden on it — contributory negligence, or that an exclusion of liability clause applies. A counterclaiming defendant bears the burden on the counterclaim.

PD 57AC DOES NOT APPLY TO EVERYTHING: it governs TRIAL witness statements in most Business and Property Courts claims from 6 April 2021. It does NOT apply to statements for INTERIM APPLICATIONS, and does not apply to the claims listed in PD 57AC para 1.3 — for example most proceedings in the Insolvency and Companies List.

body.head: WITHOUT PREJUDICE: communications made in a genuine attempt to settle are inadmissible, and a LETTER OF CLAIM should NOT contain admissions — reserve concessions for separate WP correspondence. Limited exceptions (8.13.4):
items: to explain DELAY (the fact of the communications rather than their content may suffice)
evidence of whether TERMS OF SETTLEMENT have been agreed
evidence of UNAMBIGUOUS IMPROPRIETY by a party, e.g. blackmail
evidence of MISREPRESENTATION, an ESTOPPEL or FRAUD

body: NOTICE TO ADMIT FACTS HAS COSTS TEETH: serve up to 21 DAYS before trial on Form N266. If the receiving party does not admit and the court later decides the facts SHOULD have been admitted, that party can be ordered to pay the costs of proving them — EVEN IF IT WINS the case as a whole.
REFERENCE TO A DOCUMENT TRIGGERS INSPECTION: if a document is referred to in a witness statement, witness summary or affidavit, the opposing party can require INSPECTION of it.

A DISCLOSED EXPERT REPORT BELONGS TO THE CASE: if a party decides not to rely on its expert's report after DISCLOSING it, ANY OTHER PARTY can still use it at trial. Switching experts needs the court's permission, granted only on condition the FIRST report is disclosed — and an expert merely changing their mind after meeting the opponent's expert is not usually a good enough reason.

8.9.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: SMALL CLAIMS PI FIGURES (post-Oct 2023, four tracks): small claims applies where the claim is under £10,000 AND personal-injury general damages are under: £5,000 (road traffic accident), £1,000 (vulnerable road user RTA), or £1,500 (all other PI). Tenant repair claims under £1,000 also go to small claims. Getting the £1,500 vs £5,000 split wrong is a classic trap.

INTERMEDIATE TRACK = EXPERTS, NOT 'WITNESSES': the cap is oral expert evidence limited to TWO experts per party, trial ≤3 days, value £25,000.01–£100,000. Do not confuse the expert cap with a witness cap.
COSTS ON SMALL CLAIMS TRACK: no recovery of legal costs between the parties even if you win (only fixed costs, court fees and limited expert fees). Designed for litigants in person.
COSTS BUDGETING IS MULTI-TRACK ONLY (unless the court directs otherwise): fast and intermediate track use Fixed Recoverable Costs (FRC) by complexity band, NOT Precedent H budgets.

FAILURE TO FILE A COSTS BUDGET (CPR r.3.14): the defaulter is treated as having filed a budget of applicable COURT FEES ONLY — not 'costs are assessed later'. This can wipe out recovery of legal costs.

RELIEF FROM SANCTIONS vs EXTENSION OF TIME: if you apply for an extension BEFORE the deadline, the relief-from-sanctions regime (Denton) does NOT apply. Relief is only needed once you are already in breach of a rule/order carrying a sanction.

8.8.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors

items: Is there a serious question to be tried?
Would damages be an adequate remedy for the claimant?
If not, would damages be adequate for the defendant if the injunction is granted and the claimant later loses?
Balance of convenience
Special factors (e.g. status quo). The claimant must give an undertaking in damages
body.head: AMERICAN CYANAMID TEST (INTERIM INJUNCTIONS)

items: the claimant has a good arguable case (need NOT be more than 50% prospects of success)
the defendant has assets within the jurisdiction

there is a real risk the defendant will dissipate assets — risk can be inferred from: dishonesty; past default on a debt; assets already being removed or dispersed; assets in jurisdictions where English judgments cannot easily be enforced; residence in an offshore tax haven. Worldwide freezing orders are possible but require a gateway to the foreign jurisdiction. Third parties can be joined to restrain dealing with the assets
body.head: FREEZING INJUNCTIONS: Available where

body: SEARCH ORDERS (ANTON PILLER): Require strong prima facie case, very serious potential or actual damage, and clear evidence of possession of documents/items relevant to the claim. A supervising solicitor must be present. The defendant has the right to legal advice before compliance.

INJUNCTIONS — CROWN AND PUBLIC BODIES: The Crown is not liable to injunction (Crown Proceedings Act 1947) but individual Crown servants can be injuncted in appropriate cases. Public authorities may be injuncted in judicial review proceedings.

CONTEMPT OF COURT: Breach of an injunction (or an undertaking to the court) is contempt of court, punishable by committal, sequestration of assets, or a fine. The penal notice on an injunction order must warn the respondent of this consequence.

8.7.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: BARE DENIAL IS NOT A DENIAL: r 16.5 requires REASONS, and the defendant's OWN VERSION where it intends to put one forward.

SILENCE IN THE DEFENCE = DEEMED ADMISSION. Any allegation not admitted, denied, or met by putting the claimant to proof is DEEMED ACCEPTED. Catch-all language is a safety net only — do not rely on it.

REPLY ≠ ADMISSION, BUT A PARTIAL REPLY CONCEDES. Not filing a reply admits NOTHING (r 16.7(1)). But if you DO file one and leave a point out, you are taken to REQUIRE THE DEFENDANT TO PROVE it (r 16.7).

COUNTERCLAIM vs PT 20 CLAIM: against the CLAIMANT it goes in the defence document with NO claim form. Against ANYONE ELSE a specific Pt 20 claim form is required (r 20.7), plus a response pack using the Pt 20 versions of the forms.

AMENDMENT AFTER LIMITATION EXPIRES — ONLY THREE GROUNDS: same or substantially the same facts as an existing claim; correcting a GENUINE mistake as to a party's NAME; or altering the CAPACITY in which a party claims.
AMENDING BEFORE SERVICE IS FREE BUT NOT SAFE: no consent or permission needed, but it CAN LATER BE DISALLOWED if made after a relevant limitation period ended and the opponent challenges it.
A RESPONSE TO AN RFI IS A STATEMENT OF CASE — same status as a PoC or defence, and it MUST be verified by a signed statement of truth (PD 18 para 3), served on all parties and filed.

INTEREST MUST BE PLEADED, AND ON WHAT BASIS: contract, enactment, or some other basis. For a specified sum, four further items — date from, date to (NOT LATER than issue of the claim form), total, and DAILY RATE thereafter.
WRONG COURT, WRONG SECTION: s 35A Senior Courts Act 1981 is the HIGH COURT provision; s 69 County Courts Act 1984 is the COUNTY COURT provision.
AMENDMENT LABELLING: FIRST amendments in RED, then GREEN, then VIOLET, then YELLOW — do not use red twice.
THE POC MUST NOT ANTICIPATE THE DEFENCE. Known arguments belong to the merits assessment; answer important points in the REPLY instead.

FACTS, NOT EVIDENCE: plead the facts establishing each element. Where an email exchange itself formed the contract, plead the exchange and its contents; a later email merely acknowledging a contract is evidence, not a pleadable fact.
THE DOCUMENT-REFERENCE TRAP: referring to a document in a statement of case generally DISCLOSES it — the opponent can require INSPECTION (r 31.14).

TITLE OF PROCEEDINGS: a partnership has TWO possible titles — the partners individually and numbered, OR 'AB Partners (a firm)'. A sole trader is the individual's own name 'trading as' the trading name.
SPECIALIST COURTS HAVE THEIR OWN FORMS AND LIMITS: e.g. the Commercial Court's own Pt 7 claim form N1(CC), and a 25-page / font 12 / 1.5-spacing cap.

8.6.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: THE CLOCK RUNS FROM THE PARTICULARS OF CLAIM, not the claim form. The PoC can follow the claim form by up to 14 days: r 7.4(1).

THERE IS NO 56-DAY DEADLINE IN THE CPR. 14 days to AOS; 28 days for the defence if an AOS was filed. A further agreed extension of up to 28 days is SEPARATE and does not turn the base deadline into 56.

THE AOS EXTENSION IS THE SAME WHENEVER IT IS FILED. Filing on day 1 or day 13 of the 14-day window produces the same 28-day defence deadline - so there is no advantage in waiting. THE EXCEPTION is where jurisdiction is being disputed: there the 14 days to apply runs FROM FILING THE AOS.
OUTSIDE THE JURISDICTION: use the PD 6B TABLE, do not assume 14 days. Scotland and Northern Ireland 21 days; Australia 25 days. An AOS adds 14 on top - Australia becomes 39 days.
CLAIM FORM VALIDITY: 4 MONTHS for DISPATCH within the jurisdiction; 6 MONTHS for SERVICE outside it. Do not swap these.

SUBMITTING TO THE JURISDICTION: filing an AOS confirming an intention to DEFEND, or taking any other step, loses the right to contest jurisdiction - even where there was no valid basis for jurisdiction at all. Tick the dispute box and do nothing else.
MISS THE 14 DAYS FOR THE PT 11 APPLICATION and D is DEEMED to have accepted jurisdiction.
LIMITATION IS NOT AUTOMATIC. A time-barred claim is not void - D must actively TAKE THE POINT, by applying to strike out and/or pleading limitation in the defence.
A LATE DEFENCE STILL BEATS DEFAULT JUDGMENT. D must not have filed the defence as at the date judgment is to be entered - so filing late, before judgment, prevents it.
DEFAULT JUDGMENT IS BLOCKED by an outstanding application for STRIKE OUT or SUMMARY JUDGMENT - such a defendant is challenging the claim, not ignoring it.

MANDATORY v DISCRETIONARY SET-ASIDE: r 13.2 grounds are PROCEDURAL and carry NO MERITS TEST - if the defence or AOS was already filed, the court MUST set aside. r 13.3 is where D was genuinely in default but has a REAL PROSPECT or a GOOD REASON, and there PROMPTNESS and the Denton test bite.
THE COURT MAY VARY RATHER THAN SET ASIDE under r 13.3.
COMMERCIAL COURT (Pt 58): D must acknowledge service of the CLAIM FORM even with no particulars of claim served - so default judgment can be obtained WITHOUT particulars ever being served.
A COUNTERCLAIM IS A SEPARATE CLAIM even when it operates as a defence - and D pays the SAME ISSUE FEE as if bringing fresh proceedings.
SET-OFF IS NOT AUTOMATIC: it arises where there are MUTUAL DEBTS or CLOSELY CONNECTED opposing claims, and the QUANTUM must be stated for it to work as a defence.
UNSPECIFIED-SUM DEFAULT JUDGMENT: D can still argue the AMOUNT but is precluded from arguing LIABILITY.
WITHDRAWING AN ADMISSION after proceedings have commenced needs the COURT'S PERMISSION - before commencement it needs only the agreement of the person to whom it was made.

8.4.head: ⚠ CURRENCY — conduct of litigation (examinable law update, 13 March 2026)
body: SUPERVISED DELEGATION IS LAWFUL: tasks falling within the CONDUCT OF LITIGATION may be carried out by NON-AUTHORISED persons, provided they act on behalf of and under the SUPERVISION of an authorised person (e.g. a solicitor) who retains OVERALL RESPONSIBILITY for the proceedings (Mazur v Charles Russell Speechlys LLP).
The authorised person must exercise GENUINE supervision and control. What amounts to sufficient supervision depends on the circumstances and is a matter for the regulators.
BUT: an unauthorised person CONDUCTING LITIGATION INDEPENDENTLY may commit a CRIMINAL OFFENCE under the Legal Services Act 2007.
Source: Dispute Resolution examinable law update, inserted at the end of manual section 8.4.4.2.

8.4.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: THE 100,000 THRESHOLD IS A FLOOR FOR THE HIGH COURT, NOT A CEILING FOR THE COUNTY COURT. Money claims of 100,000 or LESS should be started in the county court (PD 7A para 2.1); above that, EITHER court. The county court's jurisdiction is unlimited - it is not capped at 100,000.
PERSONAL INJURY THRESHOLD IS 50,000, not 100,000: PD 7A para 2.2.

IP GOES TO CHANCERY, NOT THE KING'S BENCH DIVISION: intellectual property disputes - copyright, patents, trade marks, registered designs, passing-off, trade secrets - belong to the Chancery Division Intellectual Property List (Patents Court or IPEC), never the KBD or the Commercial Court.
VALUE EXCLUDES interest, costs, any counterclaim, contributory negligence and any deduction of benefits. Do not add interest to push a claim over the threshold.
MUST BE HIGH COURT regardless of value: defamation, judicial review, and any claim under the Human Rights Act 1998.
ISSUING IN THE WRONG DIVISION OR SPECIALIST COURT DOES NOT INVALIDATE THE CLAIM - it is transferred, usually by consent. Do not choose an answer saying the claim is a nullity.

SPECIALIST COURTS ARE NOT SEPARATE COURTS. They are divisions and lists WITHIN the High Court. Their guides SUPPLEMENT and in places modify the CPR; they do not replace it. The Family Division is the exception - an entirely separate regime under the Family Procedure Rules 2010.

PART 8 IS ABOUT FACT, NOT VALUE OR COMPLEXITY. Use Pt 8 where there is NO SUBSTANTIAL DISPUTE OF FACT - typically a pure question of law such as the meaning of a contract term. A dispute about whether a term was breached is a Pt 7 claim.
A DEFENDANT OBJECTING TO PART 8 raises it in the ACKNOWLEDGMENT OF SERVICE; the court can then convert the claim to Pt 7 and give directions. It is not a strike-out point.

PROCEEDINGS COMMENCE WHEN THE COURT ISSUES THE CLAIM FORM - but for LIMITATION the claim is 'brought' on the earlier date the court RECEIVED it: PD 7A para 6.1. Both propositions are true; the question tells you which one it wants.

BEFORE SERVICE you usually do NOT need permission to change parties - EXCEPT to add a new CLAIMANT, which does require permission. And no one becomes a claimant without WRITTEN consent filed at court: r 19.4(4).

AFTER LIMITATION HAS EXPIRED, r 19.6 has TWO gateways (period current when proceedings started AND the change is NECESSARY) and 'necessary' has only THREE limbs - mistake in naming, claim cannot properly continue, or death/bankruptcy passing the interest. Even then the court retains a discretion; delay can defeat the application.

MISDESCRIPTION IS NOT A CHANGE OF PARTY. Getting the NAME wrong for the right legal person is cured under r 17.4(3), and can be done AFTER limitation expires if the mistake was genuine and causes no reasonable doubt about identity. Suing the WRONG PERSON is r 19.6(3) and must clear the 'necessary' test. This pair is heavily tested - e.g. an LLP sued instead of the general partnership it took over.

RELATION BACK APPLIES TO CAUSES OF ACTION, NOT PARTIES. A new cause of action added by amendment is deemed commenced when the claim was first brought; a new claim involving a NEW PARTY commences on the date that new claim is commenced: Limitation Act 1980 s 35(1). That asymmetry is the whole reason changing parties late is so restricted.
DISCONTINUANCE is the one way to remove a defendant WITHOUT permission (CPR Pt 38) - but the claimant normally pays that defendant's costs (r 38.6).
THE PARTY WHO AMENDS PAYS. The general rule is that the party seeking to amend bears the costs of and arising from the amendment, including the other parties' costs of dealing with it: PD 17.

8.3.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: LIMITATION OVERRIDES THE PDPAC. If the deadline is near or urgent relief is needed, the claimant need NOT complete pre-action steps before issuing - issue a protective claim form in time (or agree a written standstill), then seek a STAY to comply: para 17. Nothing in the PDPAC changes a limitation period.
ADR - post-CHURCHILL: a court MAY lawfully stay proceedings or ORDER the parties to engage in ADR, and unreasonable refusal can attract costs sanctions. Do NOT answer that a court cannot compel ADR.

PROFESSIONAL NEGLIGENCE IS TWO-STAGE: PRELIMINARY NOTICE first (acknowledged in 21 days), THEN a detailed letter of claim (also acknowledged in 21 days; 3 months to respond). Do not skip straight to the letter of claim. If nothing further is sent within 6 MONTHS of the preliminary notice, the claimant must notify the professional of their intentions: para 5.5.
DEBT CLAIMS applies to a BUSINESS claiming from an INDIVIDUAL, including a sole trader - NOT business-to-business. Proceedings must not start less than 30 days from the completed reply form.
RESPONSE TIME under the general PD is a 'reasonable time' - generally NO MORE THAN 3 MONTHS even in a complex case, but as little as 14 DAYS in a straightforward one. There is no single fixed period.

MOST BREACH OF CONTRACT CLAIMS have NO protocol - use the general Pre-Action Practice Direction. But a contract claim equivalent to negligence (a term to exercise reasonable skill and care) goes into the PROFESSIONAL NEGLIGENCE protocol.
DEFENDANTS have obligations too. Silence, or a negative or obstructive reply to a letter of claim or an ADR proposal, may be treated as unreasonable and attract costs sanctions.

NON-COMPLIANCE is judged on SUBSTANCE, not technicalities (para 13). The principal sanctions are on COSTS and INTEREST; strike-out is reserved for serious cases. The interest uplift against a defendant is capped at 10% ABOVE BASE RATE - not 10%.
A knowingly false statement in a pre-action letter or document prepared in anticipation of proceedings can be CONTEMPT OF COURT: para 2.
THE PDPAC IS NOT A SET OF MANDATORY RULES - but the court expects compliance and penalises its absence. Both propositions are true; an answer choosing only one is usually wrong.
AGGRESSIVE CORRESPONDENCE damages credibility, suggests a keenness to litigate rather than settle, and can itself lead to costs consequences. Assume a judge will read every pre-action letter.

8.2.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors
body: CONTRACT: DATE OF BREACH, NOT DISCOVERY. The 6-year period runs from when the cause of action accrued, i.e. the breach - not from when the buyer found out. A buyer discovering wrong goods years later must check how long ago the BREACH occurred.
TORT RUNS FROM DAMAGE, not from the negligent act. Damage is an element of the tort; it is not an element of breach of contract. This single distinction produces different answers on identical facts.

LATENT DAMAGE vs CONTRACT: more than 6 years after the events, a contract claim against a professional for want of care may be time-barred while a NEGLIGENCE claim survives under ss 14A-14B if knowledge was recent. Always test EVERY cause of action separately.
THE 15-YEAR LONGSTOP can pre-date accrual (s 14B(2)) - it runs from the negligent ACT, so a claim can be barred before any damage was even suffered. It does NOT apply to personal injury.

ACKNOWLEDGMENT RESTARTS TIME - but only if the period has NOT already expired (s 29(7)), only in debt and certain property claims (ss 29-31), and only if in writing and SIGNED (s 30; a typed name counts). Ineffective if the defendant pays part but makes clear the rest is disputed.
'BROUGHT' MEANS FILED. The clock stops when the claim form is filed or lodged with the court (PD 7A para 6.1), not on the later formal issue date. Then usually 4 months to serve.

PARTIES - TENANT SUBSTITUTION BY CONSENT: where a landlord consents, even by email, to substituting one tenant for another, that is a NOVATION and the new occupier steps into the outgoing tenant's shoes. The remaining original tenant plus the consented-in occupier are the correct defendants. An occupier who moved in without consent is NOT a party to the tenancy.

AGENTS: where the principal was DISCLOSED, sue the principal - the agent is generally not liable. Where the principal was UNDISCLOSED, the other party has a right to ELECT whether to sue the agent or the principal.

SUE THE TRUSTEES, not the trust - a trust has no legal personality. Sue the individual director? No: a director signing on behalf of a company is not the correct claimant for a breach of contract claim; the COMPANY is.

APPLICABLE LAW - IMMOVEABLE PROPERTY: under Rome I art 4(1), a contract relating to rights in immoveable property or a tenancy is governed by the law of the country where the property is SITUATED. Characteristic performance under art 4(2) is only a FALLBACK where art 4(1) gives no answer.

TORT: DAMAGE, NOT THE EVENT. Rome II art 4(1) points to where the damage occurred, and only DIRECT damage counts. A personal injury sustained in Spain is governed by Spanish law even though the lost earnings are felt in the UK.
DATE THAT MATTERS: for contracts it is the date of the CONTRACT (not the breach) that decides which regime applies; for torts it is the date of the EVENT giving rise to damage.

FOREIGN LAW MUST BE PLEADED. Absent a pleaded case to the contrary the English courts apply a PRESUMPTION OF EQUIVALENCE - that the foreign law is the same as English law. Where foreign law is in issue, expert evidence must be adduced.
The day the cause of action accrues is EXCLUDED from the calculation - unless it accrued at midnight, in which case the following day is included.

8.1.head: ⚠ MCQ Traps — Common Errors

rows: Yes - if the parties so agree
Moderator + panel of each side's executives

body: COURT CAN NOW ORDER ADR. Do NOT answer that a court cannot compel ADR. CPR r 1.1(2) makes 'promoting or using alternative dispute resolution' part of dealing with a case justly; r 1.4(2)(e) makes ordering or encouraging ADR part of active case management; Churchill confirms the court may STAY proceedings or ORDER ADR provided it does not impair the right to a judicial hearing and is proportionate.
REFUSING ADR = COSTS. A party refusing ADR without sufficient justification faces cost penalties. Parties may be required during proceedings to show ADR was duly considered.

MEDIATION IS WITHOUT PREJUDICE. Nothing said is usable on an open basis. The mediator has NO power to impose a settlement. Confidentiality depends on the parties' agreement and may not apply in all circumstances - do not state it is always confidential.
NOT BINDING UNTIL SIGNED. No settlement term agreed at a mediation binds until reduced to WRITING and SIGNED - hence the pressure to conclude on the day.

THREE grounds of challenge, not two: s 67 substantive jurisdiction, s 68 serious irregularity, s 69 point of law. Only s 69 is NON-mandatory and can be excluded by agreement - and is lost automatically if the parties dispensed with reasons under s 52. Time limit 28 DAYS from the date the arbitrator SIGNS the award (ss 70, 54(2)).
STAY IS MANDATORY, not discretionary: on a s 9 application the court MUST stay unless the arbitration agreement is null and void, inoperative or incapable of being performed: s 9(4).
'DISPUTES', not 'claims'. An arbitration clause must refer 'disputes' (s 6). Drafting it around 'claims' or 'cases' invites an argument about scope.

SEAT is not the venue. The seat is the agreed LEGAL location; hearings may be held elsewhere. Post-Arbitration Act 2025, the law of the SEAT governs the arbitration agreement itself unless the parties clearly chose another law - so English governing law + Paris seat = FRENCH law governs the arbitration clause.
LIMITATION KEEPS RUNNING during ADR. Issue a protective claim form or agree a written standstill if the clock is short (see 8.2 and 8.3).

WITHOUT PREJUDICE vs OPEN: a without prejudice communication can only be put before the court with both parties' consent; an open offer can. Costs consequences of offers are dealt with under Part 36 (see 8.16).
MEDIATION COSTS: each party bears its own costs and the mediator's fee is SHARED EQUALLY. These are NOT recoverable in later litigation absent a (very rare) specific order.
